definition_zh: 论文；专著；（专题）论著
definition_en: a long written work that examines one subject in a careful and organised way
core_image: 一本厚厚的书摊在桌上，封面标着一个题目，书页里一条条论证排得整整齐齐
scene: 导师把一本厚书推到学生面前，封面只印着一个题目。The professor pushed a bulky treatise across the desk and told her to read the chapter on soil.
sceneCN: 这里 treatise 是「专题论著」（第 1 个义项：系统论述某一主题的长篇著作）；句意：教授把一本厚厚的大部头论著推过桌面，让她先读关于土壤的那一章。

derivatives.zh: treatise 与 treat 同源自「处理」义，treat 义为「对待；处理；论述」，是去掉名词后缀 -ise 后的动词
treat + -ment 构成，义为「对待；处理；治疗」，从「怎么处理」偏移到「处理方式」
treat + -able 构成，义为「可治疗的；可处理的」，表示能够被处理
与 treatise 同出拉丁语 tractatus，义为「条约」；两词在中古英语里一度通用，后来分道

senses.title: A formal written work on one subject
senses.definition: a long book or written work that discusses one subject thoroughly and in an ordered way
senses.definitionCN: 围绕一个主题进行系统、有序讨论的长篇著作
senses.example: She published a treatise on the ecology of mountain lakes.
senses.exampleCN: 她出版了一部关于高山湖泊生态的专著。
senses.why: The Latin source tractatus means something handled or dealt with, so a treatise is a subject that has been thoroughly handled in writing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 tractatus 意为「被处理、被办理的事物」，所以论著就是把一个题目彻底处理过、写出来的成果。

senses.title: A systematic account of a field
senses.definition: a systematic account that sets out the principles and rules of a subject or craft
senses.definitionCN: 把某一学科或技艺的原理与规则系统陈述出来的著述
senses.example: Lawyers still cite the old treatise on contracts.
senses.exampleCN: 律师们至今仍引用那部古老的合同法论著。
senses.why: Medieval writers used treatise for a manual of rules, so the word kept the image of a field laid out in order, principle by principle.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪作者用 treatise 指规则手册，因此这个词保留了「一门学问按原理逐条排布」的画面。

senses.title: A long written argument
senses.definition: a long piece of writing that presents an argument at length, sometimes used slightly critically
senses.definitionCN: 长篇展开论证的文字，有时略带批评意味
senses.example: His email was less a reply than a treatise on office etiquette.
senses.exampleCN: 他那封邮件不像回信，倒像一篇关于办公室礼仪的长篇论述。
senses.why: Because a treatise is long and orderly, writers borrow it to describe any overlong argument, and the tone can turn dry or ironic.
senses.whyCN: 论著以长而有序著称，作家便借用它形容任何冗长的说理，语气也可能因此变得枯燥或带点讽刺。

intro.en: Treatise comes from Latin tractatus, a handling or discussion, from tractare, to draw out and handle.
intro.cn: treatise 来自拉丁语 tractatus（处理、论述），源于 tractare（拉扯、处理）。

items.en: Tractare means to drag, handle, or manage something.
items.cn: tractare 意为拖拽、处理或办理某事。

items.en: Tractatus names a written discussion or formal treatment.
items.cn: 约十三世纪，tractatus 指成文的论述或正式处理。

items.en: The Old French form tretiz carries the word into French usage.
items.cn: 古法语形式 tretiz 把这个词带入法语使用。

items.en: Tretys or tretis appears in English for a written account of a topic.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语出现 tretys、tretis，指对一个题目的书面论述。

items.en: The spelling treatise settles and the word narrows to a long formal work.
items.cn: 近代早期拼写定型为 treatise，词义收窄为长篇正式著作。

items.en: Modern English keeps the scholarly sense and allows a playful one.
items.cn: 现代英语保留学术义，也容许戏谑用法。

note.en: Treatise belongs to the tract- family of drawing and handling, and sits next to words for long academic writing.
note.cn: treatise 属于 tract-（拉、处理）词族，与表示长篇学术写作的词相邻。

entries.definition: to deal with or discuss a subject
entries.definitionCN: 对待；处理；论述

entries.definition: the way something is dealt with
entries.definitionCN: 对待；处理；治疗

entries.definition: a formal agreement between states
entries.definitionCN: 条约；与 treatise 同出 tractatus，但早已分化为国与国之间的正式协定

entries.definition: a long piece of academic writing based on research
entries.definitionCN: 学位论文

entries.definition: a detailed written study of a single specialised subject
entries.definitionCN: 专题研究著作； monograph 更强调单一主题的深研

entries.definition: a long essay written for a university degree
entries.definitionCN: 学位论文；长篇论述

normalIntro.en: Treatise shares the tract- root with treat and treaty: all three are about handling a matter, one in speech, one in law, one on paper.
normalIntro.cn: treatise 与 treat、treaty 共享 tract- 词根：三者都在「处理一件事」，一个用言语，一个用法律，一个用纸张。

normal.en: The verb treat means to handle a subject, and treatise is the written handling of one.
normal.cn: 动词 treat 意为处理某个题目，treatise 就是把一个题目写出来的处理成果。

normal.en: The suffix -ise here marks a noun, not a verb, so it is not British -ise spelling.
normal.cn: 这里的词尾 -ise 是名词标志，不是英式动词的 -ise 拼写。

normal.en: The fixed pattern is a treatise on something, never a treatise about something in formal writing.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 a treatise on 某主题，正式写作中一般不用 about。

normal.en: A thesis sounds personal and modern, while a treatise sounds older and more like a manual.
normal.cn: thesis 听起来更个人、更现代，treatise 听起来更古老，更像一本手册。

normal.en: Compare tractate and tract: all come from tractare, and all suggest a subject worked through by hand.
normal.cn: 对比 tractate 与 tract：都出自 tractare，都暗示一个题目被亲手反复处理。

abstract.en: Picture a very thick book whose title page shows just one subject.
abstract.cn: 想象一本很厚的书，扉页上只写着一个题目。

abstract.en: Imagine a scholar laying out rules one by one as neatly as bricks in a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象学者把规则一条条摆开，像砌墙的砖那样整齐。

abstract.en: Think of a reply that grows so long it turns into a lecture.
abstract.cn: 想象一封回信越写越长，最后变成了一场讲座。

examples.en: The museum holds a rare treatise on painting from the sixteenth century.
examples.cn: 博物馆收藏着一部十六世纪稀有的绘画论著。

examples.en: He wrote a short treatise explaining how tides worked.
examples.cn: 他写了一篇短论，解释潮汐是如何形成的。

examples.en: Students often find old treatises harder to read than modern articles.
examples.cn: 学生们常觉得旧论著比现代论文更难读。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吹题思」——对着一道题目使劲吹、用力想，写成一部长篇论著；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tractare（拉扯、处理）→ 名词 tractatus（处理；论述）→ 古法语 tretiz → 中古英语 tretis → 英语 treatise，核心义「把一个题目彻底处理成形」。

sensesIntro.en: Treatise starts with a long written work on one subject, then the systematic account of a whole field, and finally any overlong argument.
sensesIntro.cn: treatise 先指围绕一个主题的长篇著作，再指对整个学科的系统陈述，最后泛指任何冗长的论证。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick book that handles one subject from cover to cover.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本从头到尾只处理一个题目的厚书。

branches.en: The book on one subject is the base sense.
branches.cn: 单一主题的长篇著作是基本义。

branches.en: A manual of principles extends the book to a whole discipline.
branches.cn: 原则手册把这本书扩展到整个学科。

branches.en: Any lengthy argument borrows the shape of a book.
branches.cn: 任何冗长论证都借用了书的形状。

branches.en: Both are organised accounts, one of a topic, one of a field.
branches.cn: 两者都是有组织的论述，一个讲题目，一个讲学科。

branches.en: A written work can slide into an overlong argument when the tone turns dry.
branches.cn: 当语气变得干巴，成文著作就滑向冗长说理。

intro.en: Treatise is built on the Latin tract- root of pulling and handling, with English treat, treatment, tract, and treaty nearby.
intro.cn: treatise 建在拉丁语 tract-（拉、处理）词根上，周围有 treat、treatment、tract 与 treaty 等英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tractare means to drag or handle, and tractatus means the handling or the written discussion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tractare 意为拖拽、处理，tractatus 意为处理或成文论述。

items.example: The tract- root gives the pulling image.
items.exampleCN: tract- 词根给出「拉扯」的意象。

items.example: The ending -ate forms tractare from tractus.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 从 tractus 构成 tractare。

items.example: The ending -atus forms tractatus.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -atus 构成 tractatus。

items.meaning: a short written work or a stretch of land
items.example: A tract is a short treatise on a current issue.
items.exampleCN: tract 是就当下问题写的小册子。

items.example: Treat the topic with care.
items.exampleCN: 谨慎地处理这个话题。

items.example: The suffix -ment forms treatment.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ment 构成 treatment。

items.meaning: a way of dealing with something
items.example: Treatment keeps the handling sense.
items.exampleCN: treatment 保留「处理」的含义。

items.example: Treaty narrowed to a deal between states.
items.exampleCN: treaty 收窄为国家之间的协定。

items.example: Tractate is the learned twin of treatise.
items.exampleCN: tractate 是 treatise 的学术双胞胎。

definition_zh: 远足；长途跋涉；艰苦的徒步旅行
definition_en: a long and often difficult journey, especially one made on foot
core_image: 一群背着行囊的人在荒原上排成一线，脚下的路一眼望不到头
scene: 天色刚亮，队伍就背起行囊上路，脚下是碎石与荒草。They began a long trek across the plateau before sunrise.
sceneCN: 这里 trek 是「长途跋涉」（第 1 个义项：艰辛的长距离徒步旅行）；句意：天亮之前他们就开始了穿越高原的长途跋涉。

pos.zh: 远足；长途跋涉；艰苦的徒步旅行
徒步旅行；长途跋涉；艰苦地行走

derivatives.zh: trek + -er 构成，义为「徒步旅行者；远足者」，指做这个动作的人
trek + -ing 构成，义为「徒步旅行；远足活动」，作名词时常指这种运动
与 trek 同源（荷兰语 trekken「拉、迁」），义为「小径；足迹；轨道」；两词近代各自发展，拼写相近但意义已分

senses.title: A long and difficult journey on foot
senses.definition: a long journey, especially on foot, that is tiring or takes great effort
senses.definitionCN: 尤其指步行的、辛苦费力且耗费时日的长途旅行
senses.example: The trek across the desert took them ten days.
senses.exampleCN: 穿越沙漠的跋涉花了他们十天。
senses.why: The Dutch source trekken means to pull or migrate, so a trek is a pulling of oneself over long distance, step after step.
senses.whyCN: 荷兰语来源 trekken 意为「拉、迁」，所以跋涉就是一步一步把自己拉着挪过漫长路程。

senses.title: A journey loaded with belongings
senses.definition: a move of people or animals carrying their belongings over a long distance, as in an ox wagon trek
senses.definitionCN: 人畜带着全部家当长距离迁移，如牛车跋涉
senses.example: The family trekked north with two wagons and a herd of cattle.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人带着两辆马车和一群牛向北远迁。
senses.why: The word came to English from the Boers of South Africa, whose treks moved households and cattle across the veld.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由南非布尔人带入英语，他们的迁徙是带着家眷与牲口横越草原的。

senses.title: An effortful trip of everyday life
senses.definition: any long or tiring journey, often used lightly for a difficult trip like a commute
senses.definitionCN: 任何漫长或劳累的行程，常轻松地用来形容通勤之类的辛苦往返
senses.example: After the trek to the far car park, we were ready for lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 走去远处停车场这段路走完，我们已经想吃午饭了。
senses.why: Once a trek means effortful walking, speakers borrow it for a hard commute, and the tone turns friendly and exaggerated.
senses.whyCN: 既然跋涉意味着费力的行走，人们便借来形容辛苦的通勤，语气也变得亲切而夸张。

senses.title: To travel with effort
senses.definition: to make a long or hard journey, usually on foot, often without much comfort
senses.definitionCN: 作长途或艰苦的旅行，通常步行，往往缺乏舒适条件
senses.example: They trekked through the jungle for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在丛林里跋涉了三天。
senses.why: The verb keeps the motion of the noun, so to trek is to do the walking that a trek names.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了名词的运动感，trek 作动词就是去做那个名词所指的行走。

intro.en: Trek entered English from South African Dutch, where trekken means to pull or migrate; it is related to English track.
intro.cn: trek 从南非荷兰语进入英语，trekken 意为「拉、迁徙」，与英语 track 同源。

items.en: A reconstructed root for dragging or pulling lies behind the Dutch verb.
items.cn: 一个表示「拖、拉」的原始日耳曼语重构形式，是荷兰语动词的来源。

items.en: Trekken means to pull, draw, or move on.
items.cn: 荷兰语 trekken 意为拉、拽、搬动前行。

items.en: The Boers used trek for a long journey by ox wagon.
items.cn: 十九世纪，布尔人用 trek 指牛车长途迁徙。

items.en: English takes trek from Cape Dutch and writes about the Great Trek.
items.cn: 英语从开普荷兰语借入 trek，并用于记述牛车大迁徙。

items.en: Writers in India and East Africa give trek its walking sense.
items.cn: 二十世纪初，印度与东非的英语使用者赋予 trek 徒步远足的意味。

items.en: Trek becomes a noun and a verb for any long hard trip.
items.cn: 现代英语中 trek 成为名词与动词，泛指一切漫长艰苦的行程。

note.en: Trek sits with track in the pulling family of words, and next to nouns for long walks and journeys.
note.cn: trek 与 track 同属「拉、迁」词族，也与表示长途行走与旅行的名词相邻。

entries.definition: a path, a mark left by feet, or a railway line
entries.definitionCN: 小径；足迹；轨道；与 trek 同源，源自「拖、拉」

entries.definition: a person who treks
entries.definitionCN: 徒步旅行者

entries.definition: a frame of crossed bars for plants
entries.definitionCN: 棚架；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a long walk in the countryside
entries.definitionCN: 徒步；远足；比 trek 短且更轻松

entries.definition: a long walk with a fixed pace, often by soldiers
entries.definitionCN: 行军；步伐有节奏的长途行走

entries.definition: an act of travelling from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 旅程；泛指某地到某地的旅行

normalIntro.en: Trek is a pulling word: the Dutch trekken pulls a wagon, and the English trek pulls legs over long ground.
normalIntro.cn: trek 是「拉」的词：荷兰语 trekken 拉的是马车，英语 trek 拉的是两条腿走过漫长的路。

normal.en: The past tense and past participle double the final consonant, hence trekked and trekking.
normal.cn: 过去式和过去分词双写末尾辅音，所以写作 trekked 和 trekking。

normal.en: The fixed pattern is a trek through or across a place, and go on a trek.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 a trek through 某地、a trek across 某地，以及 go on a trek。

normal.en: Track and trek share the pulling root, and a track is the path a trek leaves behind.
normal.cn: track 与 trek 共享「拉」的词根，而 track 正是 trek 在身后留下的路径。

normal.en: A hike is a pleasant walk, but a trek carries weight and endurance.
normal.cn: hike 是轻松的徒步，trek 则带着负重与耐力的意味。

normal.en: The plural and the third person are both treks, so the context tells the noun from the verb.
normal.cn: 复数与三单都是 treks，要靠上下文分辨名词还是动词。

abstract.en: Picture a line of walkers with packs, shrinking small against a wide plain.
abstract.cn: 想象一队背着行囊的徒步者，在广阔平原上越走越小。

abstract.en: Imagine an ox wagon groaning across the grass with a whole household inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆牛车吱呀作响地穿过草地，车上载着整个家。

abstract.en: Think of a rainy walk from the bus stop to your door that feels far longer than it is.
abstract.cn: 想象雨后从公交站走回家的那段路，明明很短却显得特别漫长。

examples.en: The trek to the summit took two days in heavy rain.
examples.cn: 雨天里登顶的那段跋涉用了两天。

examples.en: Every summer they trek in the northern hills.
examples.cn: 每年夏天他们都在北方山区徒步旅行。

examples.en: Our trek home through heavy traffic lasted an hour.
examples.cn: 我们堵在车流里回家的那段路走了一个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特累」——背着包走一整天，特别累，就是跋涉；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 荷兰语 trekken（拖、拉、迁徙）→ 南非荷兰语 trek（牛车长途迁徙）→ 英语 trek，核心义「一步一步拉着自己走完长路」。

sensesIntro.en: Trek starts with a long hard walk, then a migration with belongings, then any tiring trip, and finally the verb of travelling so.
sensesIntro.cn: trek 先指艰苦的长途步行，再指带着家当的迁移，然后泛指任何辛苦的一趟，最后延伸为表示这样行走的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of walkers with packs crossing a wide plain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队背着行囊的人横越广阔平原。

branches.en: The long hard walk is the base sense.
branches.cn: 艰苦的长途步行是基本义。

branches.en: Migration with belongings is the historical sense.
branches.cn: 带着家当迁移是历史义。

branches.en: A tiring everyday trip borrows the word playfully.
branches.cn: 日常中辛苦的一趟借用了这个词。

branches.en: The verb carries the action of the noun.
branches.cn: 动词承接了名词所指的动作。

branches.en: Walking, migrating, and travelling all share the same slow effortful motion.
branches.cn: 步行、迁移与旅行都共享同一种缓慢费力的运动。

intro.en: Trek is a Dutch loanword built on a pulling root, with English trekker, trekking, and the related track around it.
intro.cn: trek 是建在「拉」词根上的荷兰语借词，周围有英语 trekker、trekking 与同源的 track。

latinIntro.en: Trek has no Latin root: it is Germanic and came to English through Afrikaans and Dutch.
latinIntro.cn: trek 没有拉丁词根：它属于日耳曼语，经南非荷兰语与荷兰语传入英语。

items.example: Trekken gives the pulling image.
items.exampleCN: trekken 提供「拉扯」的意象。

items.example: Trek named the Boer migrations.
items.exampleCN: trek 指布尔人的迁徙。

items.example: The suffix -er forms trekker.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 trekker。

items.example: Trekker names the walker.
items.exampleCN: trekker 指徒步的人。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms trekking.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 trekking。

items.meaning: walking in the hills for pleasure
items.example: Trekking names the activity.
items.exampleCN: trekking 指这项活动。

items.meaningCN: 双写辅音的过去式词尾
items.example: The ending -ked forms trekked.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ked 构成 trekked。

items.meaning: a path or mark left behind
items.example: Track shares the pulling root.
items.exampleCN: track 共享「拉」的词根。

definition_zh: 惊恐；惶恐；忐忑不安
definition_en: a feeling of fear or worry about something that is going to happen
core_image: 一个站在门口的人，手悬在门把上，膝盖微微发抖
scene: 面试候场区很安静，她攥着简历，手指一直在抖。She waited outside the interview room with a sense of trepidation.
sceneCN: 这里 trepidation 是「忐忑不安」（第 1 个义项：对即将发生之事的恐惧与不安）；句意：她带着一阵忐忑不安等在面试室外。

derivatives.zh: 拉丁语 trepidus（发抖的）的英语形容词，义为「惶恐的；战栗的」，多用于书面语
in-（不）+ trepid（发抖的）构成，义为「无畏的；勇敢的」，正是 trepidation 的反面
intrepid + -ity 构成，义为「无畏；勇敢」，与 trepidation 形成对照
由 trepidation 反向派生的口语化形容词，义为「忐忑的；惶恐的」

senses.title: Fear about what is coming
senses.definition: a nervous, slightly frightened feeling about something that is about to happen
senses.definitionCN: 对即将发生的事情感到紧张、略带恐惧的心情
senses.example: She opened the exam results with some trepidation.
senses.exampleCN: 她有些忐忑不安地打开了考试成绩。
senses.why: The Latin source trepidare means to hurry and tremble, so trepidation is the inner quiver that comes before an event.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 trepidare 意为慌乱发抖，所以 trepidation 就是事件来临之前内心的颤动。

senses.title: Fear in an unexpected event
senses.definition: a state of alarm or agitation caused by sudden danger or by an unexpected turn of events
senses.definitionCN: 因突如其来的危险或意外变故引起的惊恐与慌乱
senses.example: The birds flew up from the trees in great trepidation at the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟群被那声音惊得从树上慌乱飞起。
senses.why: In older medical and literary writing the word describes physical trembling and fluster, a body that has lost its steady order.
senses.whyCN: 在较早的医学与文学写作中，这个词描写的是一种身体性的发抖与慌乱，身体失去了平稳的秩序。

senses.title: A trembling movement
senses.definition: a trembling or quivering motion, mainly in older or technical writing about the body
senses.definitionCN: 身体的抖动、颤动，多见于较早的或专业性的身体书写
senses.example: The physician noted a slight trepidation of the hands.
senses.exampleCN: 医生注意到患者双手有轻微的颤抖。
senses.why: The literal sense is the shaking itself, kept in medical writing because it names the body rather than a mood.
senses.whyCN: 字面义就是「抖动」本身，医学书写保留它，是因为它说的是身体而不是心情。

senses.title: Hesitation before a step
senses.definition: a reluctance or hesitation that makes someone slow to act, often shown in speech
senses.definitionCN: 使人迟迟不敢行动的勉强与迟疑，常表现在言语当中
senses.example: He agreed, but with noticeable trepidation.
senses.exampleCN: 他答应了，却带着明显的犹豫。
senses.why: When trembling becomes visible in a voice or a pause, the fear turns into hesitation, and trepidation names that delay.
senses.whyCN: 当颤抖透过声音或停顿显露出来时，恐惧就变成了迟疑，trepidation 便指这种拖延。

intro.en: Trepidation comes from Latin trepidatio, a hurry or alarm, from trepidare, to tremble and hurry.
intro.cn: trepidation 来自拉丁语 trepidatio（慌张、惊恐），源于 trepidare（发抖、慌乱）。

items.en: Trepidare means to tremble and bustle about.
items.cn: trepidare 意为发抖、慌乱地来回动。

items.en: Trepidatio names a physical quaking or alarm.
items.cn: trepidatio 指身体性的颤抖或惊恐。

items.en: French trepidacion or Latin glossaries carry the word toward English.
items.cn: 约十五世纪，法语 trepidacion 或拉丁语注本把这个词带向英语。

items.en: Early English uses trepidation for trembling motion in astronomy and medicine.
items.cn: 早期英语用 trepidation 指天文学与医学中的颤动。

items.en: The word shifts to the emotional sense of alarm and fearful dread.
items.cn: 十七世纪，词义转向惊恐与恐惧的情绪义。

items.en: Modern English keeps a slightly formal, nervous before-an-event sense.
items.cn: 现代英语保留稍显正式、指事发之前不安的意味。

note.en: Trepidation belongs to the trembling trepid- family, and stands close to words for fear and nervousness.
note.cn: trepidation 属于表示「发抖」的 trepid- 词族，与表示恐惧与紧张的词相邻。

entries.definition: brave and unafraid
entries.definitionCN: 无畏的；勇敢的；加 in- 否定，正是不发抖

entries.definition: trembling or fearful
entries.definitionCN: 惶恐的；战栗的

entries.definition: muddy or unclear
entries.definitionCN: 浑浊的；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: anxiety that something bad will happen
entries.definitionCN: 忧虑；担心；与 trepidation 最接近

entries.definition: great fear of something in the future
entries.definitionCN: 恐惧；畏惧；比 trepidation 更强烈

entries.definition: a slight feeling of worry
entries.definitionCN: 不安；比 trepidation 更轻微

normalIntro.en: Trepidation is built on trepid, a Latin word for trembling; add in- and you get the fearless intrepid.
normalIntro.cn: trepidation 建在拉丁语 trepid（发抖）上；加上否定前缀 in-，就得到无畏的 intrepid。

normal.en: The fixed pattern is with trepidation or a sense of trepidation, rarely in the plural.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 with trepidation 或 a sense of trepidation，很少用复数。

normal.en: The noun ending is -ation, the same as fascination and hesitation, so it names a state.
normal.cn: 名词词尾 -ation 与 fascination、hesitation 相同，表示一种状态。

normal.en: Intrepid is its mirror: in- negates trepid, so a trepid person trembles while an intrepid one does not.
normal.cn: intrepid 是它的镜像：in- 否定 trepid，所以 trepid 的人发抖，intrepid 的人不发抖。

normal.en: Trepidation is more formal than fear and usually points to something about to happen.
normal.cn: trepidation 比 fear 更正式，通常指即将发生的事情带来的不安。

normal.en: Compare apprehension: both mean worried anticipation, but trepidation adds a bodily shiver.
normal.cn: 对比 apprehension：二者都指担忧的预期，但 trepidation 多了一层身体发抖的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that hovers over a door handle for one more second before turning it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在门把上多悬了一秒才拧动。

abstract.en: Imagine a room that suddenly goes silent when bad news arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象坏消息一到，整个房间突然安静下来。

abstract.en: Think of a voice that shakes slightly on the first word of a speech.
abstract.cn: 想象演讲的第一个字出口时，声音微微发颤。

examples.en: He approached the stage with considerable trepidation.
examples.cn: 他怀着相当大的忐忑走上舞台。

examples.en: There was a rumble of trepidation in the crowd when the lights went out.
examples.cn: 灯一灭，人群中响起一阵惊恐的骚动。

examples.en: She accepted the new job with a mixture of excitement and trepidation.
examples.cn: 她接受了这份新工作，既兴奋又忐忑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踹皮得身」——一脚踹过去，皮肤都在发抖，慌得不行，就是惶恐；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 trepidare（发抖、慌乱）→ trepidatio（战栗；惊恐）→ 法语 → 英语 trepidation，核心义「事情来临前身体先发抖」。

sensesIntro.en: Trepidation runs from nervous fear about what is coming, to alarm, to the trembling itself, and finally to hesitation.
sensesIntro.cn: trepidation 从对将来的紧张恐惧，到惊恐，到颤抖本身，最后到迟疑不前。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand poised on a door handle while the knees tremble.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手停在门把上，膝盖却在发抖。

branches.en: Fearful anticipation of an event is the modern main sense.
branches.cn: 对事件的恐惧预期是现代主要义项。

branches.en: Alarm from sudden danger is the stronger sense.
branches.cn: 突发危险引起的惊恐是更强的义项。

branches.en: The trembling itself is the literal body sense.
branches.cn: 颤抖本身是字面上的身体义。

branches.en: Visible trembling turns into hesitation in action.
branches.cn: 可见的颤抖会转化为行动上的迟疑。

branches.en: Anticipation, alarm, and hesitation are all forms of a body that cannot settle.
branches.cn: 预期、惊恐与迟疑都是身体无法安定的不同形态。

intro.en: Trepidation is built on the Latin trembling root trepid-, with the suffix -ation and the negated intrepid around it.
intro.cn: trepidation 建在拉丁语「发抖」词根 trepid- 上，配有词尾 -ation，周围还有否定形式的 intrepid。

latinIntro.en: Latin trepidus means trembling, and trepidare means to tremble or be alarmed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trepidus 意为发抖的，trepidare 意为发抖、惊慌。

items.example: The trepid- root gives the shaking image.
items.exampleCN: trepid- 词根给出「发抖」的意象。

items.meaningCN: 状态或过程的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms trepidation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 trepidation。

items.example: Trepid is a rare but exact adjective.
items.exampleCN: trepid 少见却精确。

items.example: The prefix in- negates trepid.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 否定 trepid。

items.meaningCN: 具有某种性质的形容词词尾
items.example: The ending -id forms adjective stems.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -id 构成形容词词干。

items.example: Intrepid means not trembling.
items.exampleCN: intrepid 意为不发抖。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms intrepidity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 intrepidity。

items.example: Intrepidity is the opposite of trepidation.
items.exampleCN: intrepidity 与 trepidation 相反。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms trepidatious.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 构成 trepidatious。

definition_zh: 擅自进入；侵入；越界；违规；罪过
definition_en: to enter someone else s land or property without permission, or to go beyond the limits that are set
core_image: 一个人翻过篱笆，闯进本不属于自己的院子
scene: 邻居的院子四周围着旧木篱笆，门口还挂着私人领地的木牌。The farmer put up a sign warning people not to trespass on his land.
sceneCN: 这里 trespass 是「擅自进入、侵入」（第 1 个义项：未经允许进入他人土地）；句意：农场主立了牌子，警告人们不要擅入他的土地。

derivatives.zh: 由 trespass 加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「非法侵入者」
动词加 -ing 构成动名词，义为「侵入行为」
由 trespass 加形容后缀 -ory 构成，义为「侵入性的」

senses.title: To enter land without permission
senses.definition: to go onto someone else s land or property without their permission
senses.definitionCN: 未经允许进入他人的土地或房产
senses.example: Two walkers trespassed on the farmer s field.
senses.exampleCN: 两名徒步者擅自进入了农夫的地里。
senses.why: The Old French word means to pass across, so trespass is literally a passing over a boundary you should not cross.
senses.whyCN: 古法语原义是「穿过、越过」，所以 trespass 字面就是越过一条不该越过的界线。

senses.title: To cross a legal limit
senses.definition: to interfere with another person s property or rights in law
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上妨碍他人的财产或权利
senses.example: Parking there is seen as a trespass on the owner s rights.
senses.exampleCN: 在那里停车被视为对业主人身财产权的侵害。
senses.why: Once crossing a boundary is wrong, the law turns the physical crossing into an offence against rights.
senses.whyCN: 一旦越界被认为不对，法律就把这一物理上的越界转化为对权利的侵害。

senses.title: To intrude on a person
senses.definition: to impose on someone or intrude on their time, privacy, or patience
senses.definitionCN: 占用他人的时间、隐私或耐心，造成打扰
senses.example: I will not trespass on your time any longer.
senses.exampleCN: 我不再占用您的时间了。
senses.why: The image moves from land to a person s private space, so to trespass on someone is to step into their territory.
senses.whyCN: 意象从土地转到人的私人空间，打扰别人就像踏进别人的地盘。

senses.title: To break a rule or limit
senses.definition: to go beyond a limit set by a rule, custom, or authority
senses.definitionCN: 超出规则、惯例或权威所设定的界限
senses.example: They trespassed against the club s ancient traditions.
senses.exampleCN: 他们违反了俱乐部古老的惯例。
senses.why: Any set line, not only a fence, can be trespassed, so the word widens to rules and customs.
senses.whyCN: 任何划定的界线不只是篱笆都可以被越过，于是词义扩展到规则与惯例。

senses.title: A sin or moral fault
senses.definition: an offence against moral or religious law
senses.definitionCN: 对道德或宗教法律的冒犯
senses.example: In the old prayer, people ask to be forgiven their trespasses.
senses.exampleCN: 在古老的祈祷文中，人们请求宽恕自己的罪过。
senses.why: Religious language treats God s law as a boundary, so a moral fault is a trespass against it.
senses.whyCN: 宗教语言把神的律法看作界线，所以道德上的过失就是对这条界线的越界。

senses.title: An act of entering unlawfully
senses.definition: the act or an instance of entering land or property without permission
senses.definitionCN: 未经允许进入土地或房产的行为或事例
senses.example: The court treated the crossing as a trespass.
senses.exampleCN: 法院把那一次穿越认定为侵入行为。
senses.why: The verb also lives on as a noun naming the act itself, the event of crossing the line.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词也用作名词，指越界这件事本身，即侵入行为。

intro.en: Trespass comes from Old French trespasser, to pass over or go beyond, built on Latin trans, across, and passus, a step.
intro.cn: trespass 来自古法语 trespasser（越过、超出），由拉丁语 trans（穿过）与 passus（一步）构成。

items.en: Trans means across or beyond.
items.cn: trans 意为穿过、越过。

items.en: Passus means a step or pace.
items.cn: passus 意为一步、一步的距离。

items.en: Trespasser means to pass over and cross a limit.
items.cn: trespasser 意为越过并跨过界限。

items.en: Trespass enters English as a word for any offence.
items.cn: trespass 在十三世纪进入英语，泛指各种过错。

items.en: Legal use fixes the sense of unlawful entry.
items.cn: 法律用法确立了「非法进入」这一义项。

items.en: Modern English keeps the physical and moral senses side by side.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留物理越界与道德越界两个义项。

note.en: Trespass is the noun and verb of crossing a boundary, close in form to trespasser and trespassing, and near in meaning to intrude and encroach.
note.cn: trespass 是表示「越过界线」的名词兼动词，与 trespasser、trespassing 形近，与 intrude、encroach 义近。

entries.definitionCN: 非法侵入者

entries.definition: the act of entering without permission

entries.definition: to move past or across
entries.definitionCN: 经过；穿过（与 trespass 共享「一步」这一词根意象）

entries.definition: to enter where you are not wanted

entries.definition: to advance gradually beyond proper limits

normalIntro.en: Trespass is a step across a line: trans, across, plus passus, a step, gives a walking over of the boundary.
normalIntro.cn: trespass 是跨过界线的一步：trans（穿过）加 passus（一步），就是走过那条界线。

normal.en: The sign says no trespassing, which means keep off the land.
normal.cn: 牌子写着 no trespassing，意思是禁止入内。

normal.en: To trespass on private land is to walk where you are not invited.
normal.cn: trespass on private land 就是走到没被邀请去的地方。

normal.en: A trespasser is the person who does it.
normal.cn: 做这件事的人就是 trespasser。

normal.en: Trans means across and passus means step, so trespass means step across.
normal.cn: trans 表示穿过，passus 表示一步，所以 trespass 表示跨过去一步。

normal.en: Compare intrude: intrude is general, trespass is often legal.
normal.cn: 对比 intrude：intrude 更泛指打扰，trespass 常带法律色彩。

abstract.en: Picture a foot lifted over a low stone wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚抬起，跨过矮石墙。

abstract.en: See a red painted line on a floor that you must not cross.
abstract.cn: 看见地板上一条红线，你不能跨过去。

abstract.en: Hear a door knock at an hour when no one should visit.
abstract.cn: 听见一个不该有人来的时刻响起敲门声。

examples.en: Visitors who trespass on the protected land are fined.
examples.cn: 擅自进入保护区的游客会被罚款。

examples.en: Please forgive my trespasses, and I will not bother you again.
examples.cn: 请原谅我的冒犯，我不会再打扰您。

examples.en: The company trespassed on its neighbors by raising the fence.
examples.cn: 这家公司把围栏加高，侵占了邻居的地界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特死怕死」——有人翻墙闯入，吓得直喊「别怕」，所以 trespass 就是擅自闯入；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 trans（穿过）+ passus（一步）→ 俗拉丁语 *transpassare（越过）→ 古法语 trespasser → 中古英语 trespass，核心义「跨过不该跨的界线」。

sensesIntro.en: Trespass begins as a physical crossing of land, widens into legal wrong, personal intrusion, broken rules, and moral sin, and also names the act as a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: trespass 先指物理上跨进他人土地，再扩展到法律侵害、侵扰他人、违反规则与道德罪过，并可用作名词指这一行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot stepping over a boundary that you do not own.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚跨过一条不属于你的界线。

branches.en: The concrete act of entering land is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 进入他人土地的具体行为是日常义项。

branches.en: Legal interference with rights grows from the same crossing.
branches.cn: 对权利的法律侵害由同一次越界生长出来。

branches.en: A person or a rule can be treated as territory.
branches.cn: 一个人或一条规则都可以被当作领地。

branches.en: Divine law as a boundary makes moral sin a trespass.
branches.cn: 把神法看作界线，道德罪过就成了越界。

branches.en: The noun names the act that the verb describes.
branches.cn: 名词义项就是动词所描述的那一行为本身。

intro.en: Trespass splits into trans, meaning across, and passus, meaning a step, with English trespasser and trespassing built around it.
intro.cn: trespass 可拆为 trans（穿过）与 passus（一步），英语围绕它构成 trespasser 与 trespassing。

latinIntro.en: Latin trans means across, and passus means a step or pace.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trans 意为穿过，passus 意为一步、一步的距离。

items.example: The prefix trans- marks the crossing.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 trans- 标示跨越。

items.example: Passus supplies the step in the image.
items.exampleCN: passus 提供了核心意象中的一步。

items.example: Trespasser is the direct French source.
items.exampleCN: trespasser 是直接的法语来源。

items.example: The suffix -er forms trespasser.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 trespasser。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms trespassing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 trespassing。

items.example: The suffix -ory forms trespassory.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ory 构成 trespassory。

items.example: Trespass keeps the crossing sense.
items.exampleCN: trespass 保留越界之意。

items.example: The noun trespass names the act.
items.exampleCN: 名词 trespass 指这一行为。

items.example: Pass shares the step and crossing root.
items.exampleCN: pass 共享「一步」与「穿过」的词根。

definition_zh: 滴流；涓涓流淌；少量渗透；零星地来去
definition_en: to flow slowly in a very thin stream, or to move slowly in small numbers
core_image: 一滴水挂在树叶尖上，慢慢地一滴一滴往下落
scene: 雨停了，屋角的水管里还有最后一滴水在慢慢往下落。A thin line of water began to trickle down the window.
sceneCN: 这里 trickle 是「细流缓慢流淌」（第 1 个义项：液体细流缓慢流动）；句意：一道细细的水流开始沿着窗户往下淌。

derivatives.zh: 由 trickle 加指小后缀 -let 构成，义为「极细的小水流」
动词加 -ing 构成动名词，义为「滴流、细流的过程」
由词组 trickle down 连字符化构成，义为「（财富）向下渗透的」

senses.title: To flow in a thin slow stream
senses.definition: to flow slowly in a very thin stream or in drops
senses.definitionCN: 以极细的水流或水滴的形式缓慢流动
senses.example: Water trickled from the crack in the old pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 水从旧管子的裂缝里细细地流出来。
senses.why: The verb imitates the repeated tiny sound of drops falling, so the core sense is liquid moving drop by drop.
senses.whyCN: 这个词模仿水滴反复落下的细小声响，所以核心义就是液体一滴一滴地移动。

senses.title: To move slowly in small numbers
senses.definition: to come, go, or pass slowly one by one in small groups
senses.definitionCN: 以很小的数量、一个接一个地缓慢来去
senses.example: Fans trickled into the stadium long before the match.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛开始前很久，球迷就陆续零零星星地进入体育场。
senses.why: People moving like drops in a thin stream produce the figurative sense of arriving or leaving slowly, one at a time.
senses.whyCN: 人流像细流中的水滴一样一个接一个，于是引申出「缓慢地零星到达或离开」的比喻义。

senses.title: To let out drop by drop
senses.definition: to cause a liquid to flow in small drops or a thin stream
senses.definitionCN: 使液体以小水滴或细流的形式流出
senses.example: She trickled oil onto the salad from a small bottle.
senses.exampleCN: 她用小瓶子把油细细地滴在沙拉上。
senses.why: The same flow can be controlled by a person, so the verb takes an object and means to let out slowly.
senses.whyCN: 同一种流动可以由人控制，于是这个动词可以带宾语，表示「使慢慢流出」。

senses.title: A thin stream of liquid
senses.definition: a small, thin flow of liquid
senses.definitionCN: 细小而细薄的一股液流
senses.example: A trickle of sweat ran down his back.
senses.exampleCN: 一股细细的汗水顺着他的背流下来。
senses.why: The action becomes a thing, so the noun names the thin stream itself.
senses.whyCN: 动作凝结成事物，于是名词指的就是那一股细细的水流。

senses.title: A small number of people or things
senses.definition: a small, slow flow of people, goods, or information
senses.definitionCN: 人数、货物或信息等的少量、缓慢的流动
senses.example: Only a trickle of applications arrived this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年只来了零零星星的几份申请。
senses.why: When the source dries up, only drops are left, so a trickle also means a very small amount.
senses.whyCN: 当源头干涸时，只剩下零星的水滴，所以 trickle 也表示极少的数量。

intro.en: Trickle is an imitative word that copies the sound of falling drops and has no Latin origin.
intro.cn: trickle 是模仿水滴落下声音的拟声词，来源不确定，并非来自拉丁语。

items.en: A Germanic group of words for drops and dripping gives the base for English trickle.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中表示「水滴、滴落」的一族词为英语 trickle 提供了基础。

items.en: The word appears meaning to fall in drops, its exact origin uncertain.
items.cn: 该词以「一滴一滴落下」的含义出现，确切来源不确定。

items.en: The verb widens to thin flowing streams and to people moving slowly.
items.cn: 现代英语中动词义扩展到细流流淌以及人缓慢移动。

items.en: The noun names the thin stream or a very small amount.
items.cn: 名词义指细小的水流或极少数量。

items.en: Economists describe money that reaches people slowly as trickling down.
items.cn: 经济学家把缓慢流到普通人手中的钱描述为向下滴流。

note.en: Trickle sits with tricklet and trickling in form, and with drip and seep in the family of slow liquid movements.
note.cn: trickle 在形式上与 tricklet、trickling 亲近，在意义上与 drip、seep 同属「液体缓慢移动」这一义场。

entries.definition: a very small trickle
entries.definitionCN: 极细小的水流

entries.definition: flowing in a thin stream
entries.definitionCN: 细细流动的

entries.definition: a clever act that deceives someone
entries.definitionCN: 诡计；诀窍（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to fall in drops
entries.definitionCN: 滴落；滴水

entries.definition: to leak slowly through small openings
entries.definitionCN: 渗出；渗透

entries.definition: to move steadily as a liquid
entries.definitionCN: 流动（比 trickle 更连续、量更大）

normalIntro.en: Trickle is the tiny brother of flow: water, people, or news arriving drop by drop.
normalIntro.cn: trickle 是 flow 的小弟弟：水、人或消息一滴一滴地到来。

normal.en: Trickle down means the liquid goes slowly from top to bottom.
normal.cn: trickle down 表示液体从上往下慢慢流。

normal.en: People trickle in when only a few arrive at a time.
normal.cn: 只有几个人陆续到达时，就是 people trickle in。

normal.en: A trickle of water is far less than a stream.
normal.cn: a trickle of water 比 stream 少得多。

normal.en: Trickling sounds like the soft plip plip of drops.
normal.cn: trickling 听起来就像水滴轻轻滴答的声响。

normal.en: Compare seep: seep soaks through material, trickle runs openly.
normal.cn: 对比 seep：seep 渗透过材质，trickle 是可见地流。

abstract.en: Picture a single drop hanging from a leaf tip, not yet falling.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗水珠挂在叶尖上，还没落下。

abstract.en: Watch the last grains of sand slide from a small hole.
abstract.cn: 看着最后几粒沙从小孔里滑落。

abstract.en: Imagine a crowd that enters a hall one person every few seconds.
abstract.cn: 想象人群每隔几秒才进去一个人。

examples.en: Blood trickled from the small cut on his hand.
examples.cn: 血从他手上小伤口里细细地流出来。

examples.en: News of the deal trickled out over several days.
examples.cn: 有关这笔交易的消息在几天里一点点传了出来。

examples.en: Rain trickled down the tent and formed a small pool outside.
examples.cn: 雨水顺着帐篷流下，在外面汇成一小洼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「翠可流」——水珠翠绿又流动得很慢，就是 trickle 细流；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为属于日耳曼语族表示「滴落」的拟声词族，可能与表示「水滴」的古词同源；确切来源不确定，并非拉丁语派生词。核心义「一滴一滴地流」。

sensesIntro.en: Trickle starts with the drop-by-drop flow of liquid and extends to people trickling in, controlled dripping, and a noun for a thin stream or a tiny amount.
sensesIntro.cn: trickle 从液体一滴一滴地流动出发，扩展到人零星地来去、使液体滴出，以及名词义的细流和极少量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop falling slowly from the tip of a leaf.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴水从叶尖慢慢落下。

branches.en: Liquid moving drop by drop is the physical sense.
branches.cn: 液体一滴一滴移动是物理义项。

branches.en: People moving like drops gives the social sense.
branches.cn: 人像水滴一样移动形成社会义项。

branches.en: Controlling the flow makes the transitive sense.
branches.cn: 控制流动就形成及物义项。

branches.en: The action turns into a noun naming the stream.
branches.cn: 动作转为名词，指那股细流。

branches.en: Drops of supply stand for a very small quantity.
branches.cn: 供给的零星水滴代指极少的数量。

intro.en: Trickle has no classical prefix, only an imitative Germanic base, with English tricklet and trickling built on it.
intro.cn: trickle 没有古典前缀，只有日耳曼拟声词根，英语围绕它构成 tricklet 与 trickling。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor for trickle, so the same-source words stay inside the Germanic and English family.
latinIntro.cn: trickle 没有拉丁语来源，同源词都留在日耳曼语与英语词族内部。

items.example: The suffix -le suggests a small repeated motion.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -le 暗示细小而反复的动作。

items.example: The suffix -et forms tricklet.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -et 构成 tricklet。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms trickling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 trickling。

items.meaning: from a higher to a lower place
items.example: Down marks the direction in trickle down.
items.exampleCN: down 标出 trickle down 的方向。

items.example: Trickle keeps the drop sense.
items.exampleCN: trickle 保留滴落之意。

items.meaning: a thin stream or small amount
items.example: The noun names the thin flow.
items.exampleCN: 名词指那股细流。

items.example: Trickling describes the sound and motion.
items.exampleCN: trickling 描述这种声响和运动。

items.example: Tricklet is the smallest member.
items.exampleCN: tricklet 是词族里最小的成员。

definition_zh: 三个月；学期；妊娠期的三个月段
definition_en: a period of three months, especially one third of a pregnancy or a school year
core_image: 日历上被直线切成三份，每份正好三个月
scene: 妇产科诊室的墙上贴着一张挂图，把整个孕期分成均等的三段。The nurse explained what to expect in the second trimester.
sceneCN: 这里 trimester 是「妊娠期的三个月段」（第 2 个义项：孕期被分成三段，每段三个月）；句意：护士解释了孕中期会出现哪些情况。

pos.zh: 三个月；学期；（孕期的）三个月段

collocations.phrase: in the first trimester of pregnancy

derivatives.zh: 由 trimester 加形容后缀 -ial 构成，义为「三个月的、学期的」
由 trimester 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「每三个月地」

senses.title: A period of three months
senses.definition: any period of three months
senses.definitionCN: 任何为期三个月的一段时间
senses.example: The clinic reviews each case every trimester.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所每三个月复查一次每个病例。
senses.why: Latin tri means three and mensis means month, so the word is simply three months.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 tri 表示三，mensis 表示月，所以这个词就是「三个月」。

senses.title: One third of a pregnancy
senses.definition: one of the three stages into which a pregnancy is divided
senses.definitionCN: 把整个孕期分成三段的其中一段
senses.example: Nausea is most common in the first trimester.
senses.exampleCN: 恶心在第一孕期最为常见。
senses.why: Medicine divides the roughly nine-month pregnancy into three equal parts, and each part keeps the name.
senses.whyCN: 医学把约九个月的孕期均分为三段，每一段都沿用这个词。

senses.title: A school term
senses.definition: one of three terms into which a school year is divided
senses.definitionCN: 把学年分成三个学期时其中的一个学期
senses.example: Students take four courses in each trimester.
senses.exampleCN: 学生每学期修四门课。
senses.why: A school year divided into three parts gives each part a three-month name.
senses.whyCN: 学年若分成三段，每段正好三个月，于是也用这个词称呼学期。

senses.title: A third of a court session
senses.definition: one of the three periods into which some legal terms are divided
senses.definitionCN: 某些法律期被分成三段时其中的一段
senses.example: The court resumes in the next trimester.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭在下一开庭期恢复审理。
senses.why: Legal calendars also cut time into blocks of about three months, so the same word appears in law.
senses.whyCN: 司法日程也把时间切成约三个月的块，于是这个词在法庭语境中也出现。

intro.en: Trimester joins Latin tres, three, and mensis, month, replacing an older classical form trimenstris.
intro.cn: trimester 由拉丁语 tres（三）与 mensis（月）结合而成，取代了更古老的形式 trimenstris。

items.en: Tres means three.
items.cn: tres 意为三。

items.en: Mensis means month, and menses means months.
items.cn: mensis 意为月，menses 意为多个月。

items.en: The classical adjective trimenstris means lasting three months.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语形容词 trimenstris 意为持续三个月的。

items.en: French forms trimestre on the model of semestre.
items.cn: 法语仿照 semestre 构成 trimestre。

items.en: English trimester first means a period of three months.
items.cn: 英语 trimester 起初指为期三个月的一段时期。

items.en: Medicine applies it to pregnancy, then schools to the academic year.
items.cn: 医学用它指孕期分段，此后学校又用它指学年分期。

note.en: Trimester shares its three-month frame with semester, term, and quarter, and its month root with menses.
note.cn: trimester 与 semester、term、quarter 同属「时间分段」义场，其「月」词根与 menses 同源。

entries.definition: one of two terms in a school year
entries.definitionCN: 半学年；学期（与 trimester 共享 mensis 月 这一词根）

entries.definition: relating to a trimester
entries.definitionCN: 三个月期的；学期的

entries.definition: happening every three months
entries.definitionCN: 每三个月一次的（与 trimester 同源，词形相近）

entries.definition: a fixed period of study in a school
entries.definitionCN: 学期

entries.definition: one of four parts of a year
entries.definitionCN: 季度；四分之一的期间

entries.definition: half of an academic year
entries.definitionCN: 半学年（两学期制中的一学期）

normalIntro.en: Trimester is three plus month: tri for three and mester from Latin mensis, month.
normalIntro.cn: trimester 就是三加月：tri 表示三，mester 来自拉丁语 mensis（月）。

normal.en: Tri comes from Latin tres, three, as in triangle.
normal.cn: tri 来自拉丁语 tres（三），就像 triangle 三角形。

normal.en: The first trimester is roughly the first twelve weeks of pregnancy.
normal.cn: the first trimester 大致是怀孕的头十二周。

normal.en: A trimester school year has three terms.
normal.cn: 三学期制的一年有三个学期。

normal.en: Semester shares the same month root and means half a year.
normal.cn: semester 共享同一个「月」词根，意思是半年。

normal.en: Compare quarter: a quarter divides the year by four, a trimester by three.
normal.cn: 对比 quarter：quarter 把一年四分，trimester 把时间三分。

abstract.en: See a cake cut into three equal slices.
abstract.cn: 想象一个蛋糕被切成三等份。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar with every three months circled in one colour.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上每三个月用同一种颜色圈起来。

abstract.en: Imagine a tiny moon chart showing a growing stomach over nine months.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅小图，显示九个月里肚子一点点变大。

examples.en: Her baby bump became visible in the second trimester.
examples.cn: 她的肚子在孕中期就显出来了。

examples.en: The college runs a trimester system, so the year has three terms.
examples.cn: 这所学院实行三学期制，所以一年有三个学期。

examples.en: Doctors check the mother once during each trimester.
examples.cn: 医生在每个孕期段里给孕妇检查一次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「揣买斯特」——怀孕要揣着宝宝，每一段都按三个月买账，所以 trimester 指三个月一段；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tres（三）+ mensis（月）→ 古典拉丁语 trimenstris（持续三个月的）→ 法语 trimestre → 英语 trimester，核心义「三个月为一段」。

sensesIntro.en: Trimester first means any three-month period, then one third of a pregnancy, a school term, and a legal session block.
sensesIntro.cn: trimester 先指任意三个月长的时期，再指孕期的一段、学期的一段，以及开庭期的一段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar chopped into equal slices of three months each.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历被切成每块三个月的等份。

branches.en: The bare three-month span is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 单纯三个月的时间跨度为字面义项。

branches.en: Pregnancy is divided into three such spans.
branches.cn: 孕期被分成三个这样的时段。

branches.en: A three-term school year uses the same unit.
branches.cn: 三学期制的学年沿用同一单位。

branches.en: Legal terms also cut time into three-month blocks.
branches.cn: 司法开庭期也把时间切成三个月的块。

branches.en: Both pregnancy and school measure progress by thirds.
branches.cn: 孕期与学期都以三等分来计量进度。

intro.en: Trimester is built from the Latin combining elements tri, three, and mester from mensis, month.
intro.cn: trimester 由拉丁语构词语素 tri（三）与来自 mensis 的 mester（月）组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin tres means three, mensis means month, and the adjective trimenstris means lasting three months.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tres 意为三，mensis 意为月，形容词 trimenstris 意为持续三个月的。

items.example: The prefix tri- gives the number three.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 tri- 给出「三」这个数。

items.example: Mensis supplies the month in the word.
items.exampleCN: mensis 提供了词中的「月」。

items.example: Trimenstris is the classical model.
items.exampleCN: trimenstris 是古典语言中的原型。

items.example: The suffix -al forms trimesterial.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 trimesterial。

items.example: The suffix -ial forms trimesterial.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ial 构成 trimesterial。

items.example: Tri- also appears in triangle and tricycle.
items.exampleCN: tri- 也出现在 triangle 与 tricycle 中。

items.example: Menses shares the month root.
items.exampleCN: menses 共享「月」这一词根。

items.example: Semester is built on the same month root.
items.exampleCN: semester 建立在同一「月」词根上。

definition_zh: 小装饰品；廉价首饰；花哨而无价值的小物件
definition_en: a small ornament or piece of jewellery of low value, often showy rather than useful
core_image: 摊开的手心上躺着一枚亮晶晶却轻飘飘的小挂坠
scene: 旅游纪念摊上，游客拿起一枚会晃动的玻璃挂坠看了看，又随手放下。At the souvenir stall, she picked up a glass trinket that swayed on its string, then put it back.
sceneCN: 这里 trinket 是「廉价小饰物」（第 1 个义项：花哨但不值钱的小摆设）；句意：在纪念品摊上，她拿起一枚会晃动的玻璃挂坠看了看，又放了回去。

collocations.zh: 小饰物与华而不实的小玩意

derivatives.zh: 由 trinket 加集合名词后缀 -ry 构成，义为「成堆的廉价小饰品」
由 trinket 与 shop 复合而成，义为「卖廉价小饰品的店铺」

senses.title: A showy but cheap little ornament
senses.definition: a small ornament, often sparkling and showy, that costs very little
senses.definitionCN: 一件小巧、闪亮好看、价钱却很低的装饰物
senses.example: The market sells wood carvings, beads and every kind of trinket.
senses.exampleCN: 集市上卖木雕、珠子和各式各样的小饰物。
senses.why: The earliest English sense already pairs smallness with low worth: a trinket is a pretty thing that has no real consequence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词进入英语时就把「小」和「不值钱」绑在了一起：trinket 首先是一件好看的、却无关紧要的东西。

senses.title: Worthless jewellery
senses.definition: a piece of jewellery made of base metal or glass rather than precious materials
senses.definitionCN: 用贱金属或玻璃而非贵金属宝石制成的首饰
senses.example: She wore a trinket round her neck instead of her mother pearls.
senses.exampleCN: 她脖子上戴的是一条廉价项链，而不是母亲的珍珠项链。
senses.why: Ornaments worn near the body narrow to jewellery, and the built-in sense of low value turns it into fake or costume jewellery.
senses.whyCN: 戴在身上的装饰物收窄成「首饰」，而「不值钱」这层含义又把它变成仿制的、装饰性的首饰。

senses.title: An object devoid of real use
senses.titleCN: 中看不中用的小玩意儿
senses.definition: a small object kept for show rather than for any practical purpose
senses.definitionCN: 只为好看而保留、并无实际用途的小物件
senses.example: Every shelf was crowded with trinkets and souvenirs nobody ever used.
senses.exampleCN: 每个架子上都挤满了从没人用过的装饰小玩意和纪念品。
senses.why: Once worthlessness is built in, the word can label any object that is decorative but useless, not only ornaments.
senses.whyCN: 既然「无价值」已是这个词的底色，它就能用来指任何只作装饰、没有用处的东西，而不限于饰物。

senses.title: Something of trifling importance
senses.definition: a minor thing or matter that carries little weight or consequence
senses.definitionCN: 分量轻、影响小的细枝末节
senses.example: Do not spend meetings debating trinkets instead of the real problem.
senses.exampleCN: 别在会议上为无关紧要的小事争论，而回避真正的问题。
senses.why: The physical smallness of the ornament becomes metaphorical: any detail too light to matter is dismissed as a trinket of a point.
senses.whyCN: 小饰物在体积上「小」，被借用来形容话题：凡轻到无足轻重的细节，都说成是一个小玩意般的问题。

senses.title: A bauble of fame or status
senses.definition: a glittering symbol of honour, success or status that is attractive but hollow
senses.definitionCN: 象征荣誉、成功或地位、耀眼却空泛的东西
senses.example: They handed out medals and trinkets until the ceremony lost all meaning.
senses.exampleCN: 他们发了勋章和一堆小饰品，直到颁奖典礼彻底变得毫无意义。
senses.why: When rewards are handed out like souvenirs, the word extends from things to social credit: honours that look bright but carry no substance.
senses.whyCN: 当奖励像纪念品一样被随手发放时，这个词从实物延伸到社会名誉：看着闪亮、内里却没有分量的荣誉。

senses.title: A trinket as a keepsake
senses.definition: a small decorative object kept to remember a place, event or person
senses.definitionCN: 为记住某个地方、事件或人而留下的小装饰物
senses.example: He kept a silver trinket from Lisbon in his coat pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 他外套口袋里一直放着一件从里斯本带回来的银色小饰品。
senses.why: The same pretty little object flips value when emotion is attached: it becomes a souvenir whose worth is memory rather than material.
senses.whyCN: 同一件好看的小东西一旦被赋予情感，价值就翻转了：它变成纪念品，价值来自回忆，而不是材质。

senses.title: A trinket held out as a lure
senses.definition: a small gift or reward offered to attract or bribe someone
senses.definitionCN: 为吸引或收买别人而抛出的小礼物或好处
senses.example: The manager dangled a bonus trinket before the sales team.
senses.exampleCN: 经理抛出一项小额奖金作为诱饵，吊着销售团队的胃口。
senses.why: A thing that is shiny and cheap is ideal for pulling attention, so the word shifts from the object held out to the act of holding it out.
senses.whyCN: 又亮又便宜的东西最适合拿来吸引目光，于是这个词从「小玩意」滑向「拿小玩意诱人」这层意思。

senses.title: A trinket judged as crude taste
senses.definition: a small decoration that signals tastelessness or cheap display
senses.definitionCN: 显示品味不高或刻意炫耀的小装饰
senses.example: The flat was lined with gilt trinkets that caught the eye of every newcomer.
senses.exampleCN: 那套公寓里摆满镀金小饰品，每个初次来访的人都会被它们吸引。
senses.why: Because a trinket is all surface, it can also judge taste: a room full of them reads as cheap and loud rather than rich.
senses.whyCN: trinket 只有表面、没有内里，因此它也能用于评判品味：满屋子这样的东西，显得廉价喧闹，而不是富足。

intro.en: Trinket is first recorded in English in the mid sixteenth century, and its earlier source is uncertain; the most widely repeated suggestion is a link with an old word for a trifle or knick-knack rather than a descent from Latin.
intro.cn: trinket 最早见于十六世纪中叶的英语，更早的来源不确定；流传最广的说法是它与某个表示「小玩意儿」的旧词有关，而非直接来自拉丁语。

items.en: The origin of trinket is uncertain; no Latin verb or noun is securely agreed to underlie it.
items.cn: trinket 的来源不确定，学界尚无公认可靠的拉丁语动词或名词作为其词基。

items.en: One suggestion links it to a word for a pleasing little thing; the borrowing path is disputed.
items.cn: 一种说法认为它与法语中表示「讨喜小物」的词有关；借用路径仍有争议。

items.en: Trinket is recorded in English from the mid sixteenth century with the meaning of a small ornament.
items.cn: 十六世纪中叶，trinket 已在英语中记录为「小装饰品」。

items.en: The word is applied to cheap jewellery and to any showy but useless object.
items.cn: 到十八九世纪，这个词被用于廉价首饰，以及任何花哨而无用的物件。

items.en: Modern English extends trinket to figurative tokens of status and to trivial matters.
items.cn: 现代英语把 trinket 扩展到比喻性的荣誉象征和无关紧要的琐事。

note.en: Trinket sits among small-object words, close in form to ringing words such as trinketry, and close in meaning to cheap ornament and knick-knack words.
note.cn: trinket 属于「小物件」词族，形式上与 trinketry 这类同类词相近，意义上贴近「廉价饰物」「小玩意」的同类词。

entries.definition: cheap trinkets as a group
entries.definitionCN: 成群成堆的小饰物

entries.definition: a shop that sells cheap ornaments
entries.definitionCN: 售卖廉价小饰品的店铺

entries.definition: a small box for keeping ornaments
entries.definitionCN: 装小饰品的盒子；只是复合表达，词源与其他条目不同

entries.definition: a showy ball-shaped ornament of little value
entries.definitionCN: 华而不实、不值钱的小装饰品

entries.definition: a decorative object of any value
entries.definitionCN: 装饰品；泛指装饰，不代表廉价

entries.definition: a small decorative object of little worth
entries.definitionCN: 小玩意；小摆设

entries.definition: an object kept to remember a place or event
entries.definitionCN: 纪念品，重在回忆而非材质

normalIntro.en: Trinket is a small, bright sound for a small, bright thing: think of a charm that tinkles when it swings.
normalIntro.cn: trinket 的读音清脆轻巧，正好配「小而亮」的东西：想象一枚小挂坠晃动摇响。

normal.en: Trinkets are cheap: a trinket is small and pretty, not precious.
normal.cn: trinket 很便宜：小而好看，但不贵重。

normal.en: A trinket box keeps small ornaments tidy.
normal.cn: trinket box 用来收纳小饰品。

normal.en: The plural is trinkets, as in shelves full of trinkets.
normal.cn: 复数是 trinkets，如摆满小饰品的架子。

normal.en: The suffix -ry makes trinketry, the whole heap of ornaments.
normal.cn: 加上后缀 -ry 成为 trinketry，指一整堆小饰品。

normal.en: Compare bauble: both mean cheap ornaments, but bauble often suggests a round glass bauble.
normal.cn: 对比 bauble：两者都指廉价饰物，但 bauble 常暗示玻璃圆球。

abstract.en: Picture a tourist holding up a glass charm to the sun.
abstract.cn: 想象游客把一枚玻璃小挂坠对着阳光举起来。

abstract.en: Imagine a drawer of earrings that tarnish within a week.
abstract.cn: 想象一抽屉戴一周就发黑的耳环。

abstract.en: Think of a shelf that looks full but holds nothing you need.
abstract.cn: 想象一个看着满满当当、却没有一件用得上的架子。

examples.en: The stall was covered with trinkets made of painted glass.
examples.cn: 摊子上摆满了彩绘玻璃做的小装饰品。

examples.en: She bought a brass trinket for her little sister.
examples.cn: 她给妹妹买了一个黄铜小饰品。

examples.en: Tourists often collect cheap trinkets as reminders of a trip.
examples.cn: 游客常收集廉价小玩意儿，作为旅行的纪念。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「叮当一串」——一串小挂件晃起来叮当响，就是廉价小饰物；这只是谐音联想，与真实的词源无关。

root: 来源不确定：一般认为 trinket 是十六世纪英语中出现的小物件词，可能受某种表示「小玩意」的旧词影响；它与拉丁语无明显同源关系，应按「来源不详」理解，不宜强行拆成词根。

sensesIntro.en: Trinket starts from a cheap ornament and then widens in two directions: to any useless pretty object, and to figurative tokens of status that glitter but carry no weight.
sensesIntro.cn: trinket 从「廉价小饰物」出发，向两个方向扩展：一是任何好看却无用的小物件，二是闪亮却没有分量的荣誉象征。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small bright ornament that looks precious but is worth almost nothing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件小而闪亮、看着像宝贝却几乎不值钱的饰物。

branches.en: A small cheap ornament is the literal, concrete sense.
branches.cn: 小而廉价的装饰品是字面的具体义项。

branches.en: Jewellery narrows the object to what is worn on the body.
branches.cn: 首饰义项把物件收窄到戴在身上的东西。

branches.en: Uselessness generalises the ornament to any decorative object.
branches.cn: 无用义项把小饰物推广到任何装饰性物件。

branches.en: Figurative trinkets describe trivia and hollow honours.
branches.cn: 比喻用法指琐碎之事和空洞的荣誉。

branches.en: Souvenir, lure and bad taste all depend on how a cheap object is used.
branches.cn: 纪念物、诱饵与俗气品味，都取决于这件廉价物件被如何使用。

intro.en: Trinket derives no clean prefixes or suffixes; its English family is built with -ry, with compounds, and with the plural -s.
intro.cn: trinket 并没有清晰的派生前缀或后缀；它的英语词族靠 -ry 后缀、复合词和复数 -s 构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no secure Latin ancestor for trinket, so the Latin list stays empty and the forming parts are English only.
latinIntro.cn: trinket 没有可靠的拉丁语祖词，所以拉丁同源词表留空，构词部件全部属于英语。

items.example: Trinket is the base form of the family.
items.exampleCN: trinket 是这个词族的基础形式。

items.example: The suffix -s makes trinkets.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 trinkets。

items.example: The suffix -ry forms trinketry.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ry 构成 trinketry。

items.example: Trinketry names the heap rather than one piece.
items.exampleCN: trinketry 指一整堆，而不是单件。

items.example: Shop combines to form trinketshop.
items.exampleCN: shop 复合成 trinketshop。

items.example: Trinketshop is a compound of two nouns.
items.exampleCN: trinketshop 是由两个名词组成的复合词。

items.example: Box combines to form trinket box.
items.exampleCN: box 组成 trinket box。

items.example: Trinket box uses the word as a modifier.
items.exampleCN: trinket box 中 trinket 作修饰语。

items.example: Glass trinkets are typical of souvenir stalls.
items.exampleCN: 玻璃小饰品是纪念品摊的典型货品。

definition_zh: 三倍的；三重的；（使）增至三倍；三连冠
definition_en: consisting of three parts or three times as much, or to make or become three times as large
core_image: 同一个轮廓在眼前稳稳地叠成三层
scene: 新厂房投产后，这家工厂的玻璃产量一下子涨到原来的三倍。Output tripled after the new plant opened, and the glass works now runs three shifts.
sceneCN: 这里 triple 是「增至三倍」（第 3 个义项：数量变为原来的三倍）；句意：新工厂开工后，产量增至三倍，玻璃厂现在开三班。

pos.zh: 三倍的；三重的；由三部分组成的

derivatives.zh: triple 加指小后缀 -et 构成，义为「三胞胎之一」「三个一组中的一个」
源自拉丁语 triplicare（叠成三重），义为「一式三份」
拉丁语 triplex（三重的）直系借入，义为「三重的」「三层住宅」

senses.title: Three times as much
senses.definition: being three times the usual size, amount or number
senses.definitionCN: 达到通常大小、数量或数目三倍的
senses.example: A triple portion of rice kept the whole crew going.
senses.exampleCN: 一份三倍的米饭让全体船员撑了下来。
senses.why: The Latin root tri- carries the idea of three, and the -ple ending marks a fold, so triple names a quantity folded three times over.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 tri- 表示「三」，-ple 词尾表示「叠」，所以 triple 就是被叠了三次、放大了三倍的量。

senses.title: Having three parts
senses.definition: made of or involving three parts, layers or stages
senses.definitionCN: 由三部分组成，或涉及三层、三阶段的
senses.example: They installed triple glazing to keep out the winter wind.
senses.exampleCN: 他们装上三层玻璃，抵御冬天的风。
senses.why: Three folds of any material become three layers, so triple moves from pure quantity to structure with three parts.
senses.whyCN: 任何材料叠三次就成了三层，triple 于是从单纯的「量」走到「由三部分组成的结构」。

senses.title: To make three times larger
senses.definition: to increase an amount, output or price to three times its former level
senses.definitionCN: 把数量、产量或价格提高到原来的三倍
senses.example: The firm plans to triple its spending on research next year.
senses.exampleCN: 公司计划明年把研发支出增至三倍。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a verb with no extra ending: triple is what you do when you fold a quantity three times.
senses.whyCN: 形容词无须加后缀就直接转动词：把一个量叠三次，就是 triple。

senses.title: To grow three times over
senses.definition: to become three times as large without an outside agent
senses.definitionCN: 在没有外来施动者的情况下自身变为原来的三倍
senses.example: Tourist numbers tripled during the festival month.
senses.exampleCN: 节庆月里游客人数增至三倍。
senses.why: The same verb works intransitively: the quantity folds itself, and English does not need to add a suffix for that shift.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词也可不及物使用：数量自行翻倍，英语不需要为这一转换另加词尾。

senses.title: Three successive wins
senses.definition: a set of three successes or titles won one after another
senses.definitionCN: 连续获得的三次胜利或三个冠军头衔
senses.example: The club completed the triple before a home crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部在主场观众面前拿下三连冠。
senses.why: When success comes three times in a row, names the run in sports are borrowed from the number three itself.
senses.whyCN: 胜利连续出现三次时，体育界直接用「三」来命名这一串成绩。

senses.title: Three of the same kind
senses.definition: a group of three people or things of the same kind, especially in a pattern
senses.definitionCN: 三个同类人或物组成的一组，尤指有规律的组合
senses.example: The design repeats a triple of blue stripes on the sleeve.
senses.exampleCN: 袖口上重复着三蓝条纹的组合。
senses.why: Counting three equal things together is the most basic use of the number, and triple keeps that grouping sense in names and patterns.
senses.whyCN: 把三个相同之物放在一起数，是「三」最基本的用法，triple 在名称和花纹中保留了这种成组含义。

senses.title: Triple in music
senses.definition: a rhythm in which each bar is divided into groups of three beats
senses.definitionCN: 每小节按三拍分组的节奏
senses.example: The waltz moves in a triple time that dancers feel at once.
senses.exampleCN: 华尔兹是三拍子，舞者一听就能感觉到。
senses.why: A beat grouping into three is felt as one musical unit, so the number three becomes a name for the metre.
senses.whyCN: 以三拍为一组，在听觉上构成一个完整的音乐单位，于是「三」成为节拍的名称。

senses.title: Triple in chemistry
senses.definition: a term for a bond of three pairs of shared electrons or for a cell with three chromosomes
senses.definitionCN: 指三对共享电子构成的化学键，或指有三套染色体的细胞
senses.example: The triple bond in the nitrogen molecule makes it very stable.
senses.exampleCN: 氮分子中的三键让它非常稳定。
senses.why: Precise scientific naming keeps the same strategy: whatever comes in threes of the same kind is called triple for that feature.
senses.whyCN: 科学命名沿用同一套思路：凡是三份相同之物构成的，就用 triple 称呼这一特征。

intro.en: Triple comes from Latin triplus, a fold of three, from tri- three and the root of plicare, to fold; the verb triplicare, to fold threefold, supplies the English verb.
intro.cn: triple 来自拉丁语 triplus（三折），由 tri-（三）与 plicare（折叠）的词根构成；动词 triplicare（折成三重）提供了英语的动词义。

items.en: Reconstructed forms for three underlie the Latin tri- found in triple.
items.cn: 「三」的原始印欧语重构形式，是 triple 中拉丁 tri- 的源头。

items.en: Triplus joins tri-, three, to the folding root of plicare, so a triple is something folded three times.
items.cn: triplus 把 tri-（三）与 plicare 的「折」词根结合起来，所以三重之物就是被折了三次的东西。

items.en: Triplicare is a verb meaning to fold into three folds or to increase threefold.
items.cn: triplicare 是动词，意为折成三重或增至三倍。

items.en: Adjective and verb forms enter French as triple and tripler.
items.cn: 形容词和动词形式以 triple、tripler 进入法语。

items.en: Triple appears in English as both adjective and verb, keeping the ideas of threefold and of tripling.
items.cn: triple 以形容词和动词两种身份进入英语，保留了「三倍」和「增至三倍」两层含义。

items.en: Modern English uses triple for layers, records, metres and chemical bonds.
items.cn: 现代英语用 triple 表示层数、纪录、格律和化学键。

note.en: Triple belongs to the Latin number-three family, together with triplet, triplicate and triplex, and to counting words such as double and quadruple.
note.cn: triple 属于拉丁语的「三」词族（triplet、triplicate、triplex），也贴近 double、quadruple 这类倍数词。

entries.definition: one of three children born together
entries.definitionCN: 三胞胎中的一个

entries.definition: made or kept in three copies
entries.definitionCN: 一式三份的

entries.definition: threefold, or a building of three dwellings
entries.definitionCN: 三重的；三层或三联住宅

entries.definition: twice as much
entries.definitionCN: 两倍的

entries.definition: four times as much
entries.definitionCN: 四倍的

entries.definition: three times as great
entries.definitionCN: 三倍的，较书面

entries.definition: the British form of the threefold adjective and verb
entries.definitionCN: 英式拼写，义同三倍、增至三倍

normalIntro.en: Triple carries tri-, the Latin mark of three, plus an ending that means fold, so it always means three layers or three times.
normalIntro.cn: triple 里有表示「三」的拉丁词根 tri-，加上意为「叠」的词尾，所以它总意味着三层或三倍。

normal.en: tri- means three, as in triangle and tricycle.
normal.cn: tri- 表示三，如三角形和三轮车。

normal.en: Remember the fold in triple with the ending -ple seen in double.
normal.cn: triple 的「叠」与 double 的结尾 -ple 同理。

normal.en: Triple works as adjective, verb and noun with one spelling.
normal.cn: triple 一个拼写兼作形容词、动词和名词。

normal.en: The verb changes to tripled, tripling and triples.
normal.cn: 动词变为 tripled、tripling、triples。

normal.en: Compare treble in British usage and quadruple for four times.
normal.cn: 对比英式 treble，以及表示四倍的 quadruple。

abstract.en: Picture three identical panes stacked in one window frame.
abstract.cn: 想象三块一模一样的玻璃叠在一个窗框里。

abstract.en: Imagine a bar chart where one column grows to three times its height.
abstract.cn: 想象柱状图里一根柱子长到原来的三倍高。

abstract.en: Think of a champion lifting the same cup for the third year.
abstract.cn: 想象冠军连续第三年举起同一座奖杯。

examples.en: Rent tripled in the five years after the metro line opened.
examples.cn: 地铁线路开通后的五年里，房租涨到了三倍。

examples.en: The triple windows keep the studio warm all winter.
examples.cn: 三层玻璃窗让工作室整个冬天都很暖和。

examples.en: Their profits grew to triple the level of the previous decade.
examples.cn: 他们的利润增长到此前十年的三倍水平。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吹不破」——一层玻璃吹不破，就叠三层；借「三」的读音记住三倍、三重；这只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 tri-（三）+ plicare（折叠）→ triplus（三重的）→ 古法语 triple → 英语 triple；-ple 同源于「折叠」，与 double、quadruple 构成倍数系列。

sensesIntro.en: Triple begins as the number three turned into a multiple, then splits into three parts or layers, into the verb for tripling, and into fixed names in sport, music and science.
sensesIntro.cn: triple 从「三」变为倍数开始，再分化为三部分或三层、动词「增至三倍」，以及体育、音乐、科学中的固定名称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one shape folded over itself until three layers sit exactly on top of each other.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个形状被折叠，最后三层严丝合缝地叠在一起。

branches.en: Three times as much is the basic multiple sense.
branches.cn: 三倍是基本的倍数义项。

branches.en: Three parts or layers is the structural sense.
branches.cn: 三部分或三层是结构义项。

branches.en: The verb covers both making and becoming threefold.
branches.cn: 动词义兼指使增三倍和自增至三倍。

branches.en: Names for three wins and for a group of three.
branches.cn: 指三连冠和三个一组。

branches.en: Fixed terms in music and chemistry keep the same count of three.
branches.cn: 音乐与化学的固定术语同样数着「三」。

intro.en: Triple is built from the Latin prefix tri- and a fold-related ending, and English adds -et, -ate and -ex through related borrowings.
intro.cn: triple 由拉丁前缀 tri- 与表示「折叠」的词尾构成，英语又通过与它同族的借词加入 -et、-ate、-ex 等形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin tri- means three and plicare means to fold, giving triplus and triplicare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tri- 意为三，plicare 意为折叠，由此产生 triplus 与 triplicare。

items.example: The prefix tri- appears in triangle.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 tri- 见于 triangle。

items.example: Triplus is the direct source of triple.
items.exampleCN: triplus 是 triple 的直接来源。

items.example: Triplicare feeds the English verb sense.
items.exampleCN: triplicare 提供了英语的动词义。

items.example: The ending -ple is shared with double.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ple 与 double 共用。

items.example: Triple keeps all three parts of speech.
items.exampleCN: triple 兼有三种词性。

items.example: The suffix -et forms triplet.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -et 构成 triplet。

items.example: Triplet names a single member of three.
items.exampleCN: triplet 指三人中的一个。

items.example: Triplex is a direct Latin borrowing.
items.exampleCN: triplex 是直接借自拉丁语的形式。

items.meaningCN: 构成特定状态的分词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ate forms triplicate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成 triplicate。

latinEntries.example: Tri is the numeral behind every word here.
latinEntries.exampleCN: tri 是这一族词背后的数词。

latinEntries.example: Triplex was borrowed directly into English.

definition_zh: 胜利的；得意扬扬的；欢庆胜利的
definition_en: having won a victory, or showing great joy and pride because of a victory
core_image: 一个人高举手，从欢呼的人群中间走过
scene: 终场哨响，球员冲上看台，主教练举起双臂向观众示意。When the final whistle blew, the triumphant coach raised both arms toward the crowd.
sceneCN: 这里 triumphant 是「胜利的」（第 1 个义项：取得胜利的）；句意：终场哨响后，这位胜利的主教练向观众举起双臂。

derivatives.zh: 去掉形容词后缀 -ant 后的基础词，义为「胜利；获胜」
triumphant 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「胜利地；得意地」
与 triumphant 同源的形容词，义为「凯旋的；庆祝胜利的」

senses.title: Having won a victory
senses.definition: having defeated an opponent or achieved a hard goal
senses.definitionCN: 击败对手或达成一个艰难目标的
senses.example: The triumphant side left the field to a wall of noise.
senses.exampleCN: 获胜的一方在一片欢呼声中离场。
senses.why: The Latin triumphus named the ceremonial entry of a victorious general, so the word carried winning from the start.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 triumphus 本指凯旋将军的正式入城仪式，因此这个词从一开始就带着「胜利」的核心。

senses.title: Showing joy and pride
senses.definition: openly showing delight and self-satisfaction after a success
senses.definitionCN: 在成功后公开表现出喜悦与自得
senses.example: She gave a triumphant grin as the last card fell into place.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一张牌摆对位置时，她露出得意的笑。
senses.why: A public procession makes the winner visible to everyone, so the same word moves from the result to the face and body showing it.
senses.whyCN: 游行使胜者现身于众人面前，于是同一个词从「结果」转向表现结果的神情与姿态。

senses.title: Celebrating a victory
senses.definition: used for the ceremony, speech or march that marks a victory
senses.definitionCN: 用于庆祝胜利的仪式、演说或游行
senses.example: Crowds lined the road for the triumphant march through the old quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 人们沿路夹道，观看穿过老城区的凯旋游行。
senses.why: The victory parade is the most literal echo of the Roman rite, and any ceremony modelled on it keeps the word.
senses.whyCN: 凯旋游行最直接地保留了古罗马仪式的影子，凡是仿此而办的庆典都沿用这个词。

senses.title: Overcoming a long struggle
senses.definition: achieving success after a long and difficult fight, especially against illness or hardship
senses.definitionCN: 在长期艰难的抗争（如疾病或困境）之后终于获得成功
senses.example: After two years of treatment she made a triumphant return to work.
senses.exampleCN: 经过两年的治疗后，她重归工作岗位，光彩照人。
senses.why: The ancient victory followed a battle, so the word easily stretches to wins over suffering where no opponent is visible.
senses.whyCN: 古代的胜利总是在一场战斗之后到来，因此这个词很容易延伸到没有明确对手、只与苦难较量的胜利。

senses.title: Exultant in speech
senses.titleCN: 语气高涨的；志得意满的
senses.definition: describes words, music or tone that sound like a shout of victory
senses.definitionCN: 形容言辞、音乐或语调如同胜利的呼喊
senses.example: The letter ended on a triumphant note of certainty.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信在一种自信的、胜利般的语气中收尾。
senses.why: A shout of victory is a sound before it is a statement, so triumphant can colour any sound that rises like a cheer.
senses.whyCN: 胜利的呼喊首先是一种声音，然后才是话语，所以 triumphant 可以给任何像欢呼一样上扬的声音染色。

intro.en: Triumphant comes from Latin triumphare, to celebrate a triumph, built on triumphus, the victory procession of a Roman general; the noun triumph passed through Old French into English, and the adjective was made in English with the suffix -ant.
intro.cn: triumphant 来自拉丁语 triumphare（庆祝凯旋），其词基 triumphus 指古罗马将军的凯旋仪式；名词 triumph 经古法语进入英语，形容词则用后缀 -ant 在英语中构成。

items.en: Triumphus names the ceremonial procession of a victorious Roman commander.
items.cn: triumphus 指罗马得胜统帅的凯旋游行仪式。

items.en: The further origin of triumphus is disputed; it may be a borrowing from Etruscan or Greek, and no secure Latin root is agreed.
items.cn: triumphus 的更早来源有争议，可能借自伊特鲁里亚语或希腊语，尚无公认可靠的拉丁词根。

items.en: Triumphare, to celebrate a triumph, turns the ceremony into a verb.
items.cn: triumphare（庆祝凯旋）把这个仪式变成动词。

items.en: Old French triumphe / triomphe carries the noun into French from Latin.
items.cn: 古法语 triumphe、triomphe 把这一名词从拉丁语带入法语。

items.en: The noun triumph enters English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 triumph 于十四世纪进入英语。

items.en: The adjective triumphant is formed in English with the suffix -ant on the model of the Latin participle.
items.cn: 形容词 triumphant 在英语中仿照拉丁分词，用后缀 -ant 构成，约见于十六世纪。

note.en: Triumphant is the adjective of the triumph family, alongside triumph and triumphantly, and it also sits close to other words for victory and for open delight.
note.cn: triumphant 是 triumph 词族的形容词，与 triumph、triumphantly 同族，也贴近其他表示「胜利」和「喜不自胜」的词。

entries.definition: in a triumphant way
entries.definitionCN: 胜利地；得意地

entries.definition: relating to a victory celebration
entries.definitionCN: 凯旋的；为庆祝胜利的

normalIntro.en: Triumphant is triumph plus the adjectival -ant, so it means the quality of triumph at any moment of a victory.
normalIntro.cn: triumphant 是 triumph 加形容词后缀 -ant，表示在胜利某个时刻所带有的那种「得胜」性质。

normal.en: triumph + -ant gives the adjective triumphant.
normal.cn: triumph 加 -ant 构成形容词 triumphant。

normal.en: Add -ly to get the adverb triumphantly.
normal.cn: 再加 -ly 得到副词 triumphantly。

normal.en: The base noun triumph keeps the harder ending -ph.
normal.cn: 基础名词 triumph 保留更重的 -ph 结尾。

normal.en: A triumphant return means a comeback after many problems.
normal.cn: a triumphant return 指历经曲折后的凯旋归来。

normal.en: Triumph traces back to the Roman victory parade, called a triumphus.
normal.cn: triumph 可追溯到古罗马的凯旋游行 triumphus。

abstract.en: Picture a runner breaking the tape with arms flung wide.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者张开双臂冲过终点线。

abstract.en: Imagine a face lit up by a grin that cannot be hidden.

abstract.en: Think of confetti falling over a crowd that has just won.
abstract.cn: 想象彩纸从刚刚获胜的人群头顶落下。

examples.en: The team returned home triumphant after the away win.
examples.cn: 球队在客场取胜后凯旋归来。

examples.en: He gave me a triumphant look after the argument.
examples.cn: 争论结束后，他得意地看了我一眼。

examples.en: A triumphant crowd gathered in the square to hear the news.
examples.cn: 欢庆的人群聚集在广场上听这个消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拽象飞」——有人拽着大象飞了起来，一副得胜得意的样子；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

sensesIntro.en: Triumphant starts from the winner of a contest, spreads to the joy that a win shows on a face, to the ceremony that marks it, and to hard-won comebacks and exultant sounds.
sensesIntro.cn: triumphant 从「比赛的胜者」出发，扩展到胜利写在脸上的喜悦、标记胜利的仪式，以及艰难赢得的归来与高扬的声音。

core.cn: 核心意象：胜者高举双臂走出人群，两旁欢呼四起。

branches.en: Having won is the literal result sense.
branches.cn: 获胜是字面的结果义项。

branches.en: Visible pride in a face is the emotional sense.
branches.cn: 写在脸上的自得是情绪义项。

branches.en: The procession and its ceremonies keep the ancient rite.
branches.cn: 游行与相关仪式保留了古代礼制。

branches.en: Long struggles such as illness produce a harder kind of triumph.
branches.cn: 疾病等长期抗争带来一种更艰难的胜利。

branches.en: An exultant tone borrows the sound of a cheer.
branches.cn: 沸腾的语气借用的是欢呼的声音。

intro.en: Triumphant is an English adjective built with the suffix -ant on the triumph family, which shares the Latin stem triumph- with triumph and triumphal.
intro.cn: triumphant 是用后缀 -ant 在 triumph 词族上构成的英语形容词，与 triumph、triumphal 共享拉丁词干 triumph-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stem triumph- comes from triumphus, the victory rite, and its own earlier origin is disputed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词干 triumph- 来自 triumphus（凯旋礼），而它更早的来源尚有争议。

items.meaningCN: 形容词后缀，表示「处于某状态」

items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 构成 triumphant。

items.example: Triumphant describes the winning state.
items.exampleCN: triumphant 描述得胜状态。

items.example: The suffix -al forms triumphal.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 triumphal。

items.example: Triumphal is used for the ceremony, not the person.
items.exampleCN: triumphal 多用于仪式，而非人。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms triumphantly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 triumphantly。

items.example: Triumphantly modifies how someone acts.
items.exampleCN: triumphantly 修饰人的行为方式。

items.example: Triumphus is the Latin starting point.
items.exampleCN: triumphus 是拉丁语起点。

items.exampleCN: triumphare 提供词族的动词一侧。

definition_zh: 使显得琐碎；轻视；淡化，把严重问题说成小事
definition_en: to make something seem less important, serious, or difficult than it really is
core_image: 一座坚固的塔楼被拆成三岔路口边的小石头，严重的分量一下子缩成碎屑
scene: 会议上，经理把整个团队的加班事故说成小插曲，大家听了都很不舒服。At the meeting, the manager trivialized the accident by calling it a small episode.
sceneCN: 这里 trivialize 是「淡化、把严重的事说成小事」（第 1 个义项：把重要的事说成不重要）；句意：会上经理把事故说成小插曲，实际上是在淡化它的严重性。

pos.zh: 使显得琐碎；轻视；淡化（严重性）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「轻视化；淡化」
基础形容词，义为「琐碎的；不重要的」
形容词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「琐事；无足轻重」
形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「轻而易举地；琐碎地」
trivial 加否定前缀 non-，数学与计算机语境中指「不简单的；有实质难度的」

senses.title: To make something seem unimportant
senses.definition: to treat or describe something significant as if it were small and unimportant
senses.definitionCN: 把重要或严重的事情说成、当成小事
senses.example: Critics say the film trivializes a real disaster.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说这部影片把一场真实的灾难拍得像个笑话。
senses.why: The Latin base trivialis meant belonging to the crossroads, and by extension the common and small, so to make something seem like that is to shrink its weight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词干 trivialis 原指属于三岔路口、街头巷尾的，引申为「平常琐碎」，所以把某事说成像那样，就是把它的分量压小。

senses.title: To reduce to trifles in discussion
senses.titleCN: 轻描淡写；说得不值一提
senses.definition: to describe an issue in terms so slight that its importance is lost in the telling
senses.definitionCN: 用极轻的说法谈论事态，使其重要性在叙述中被抹掉
senses.example: Do not trivialize the pain of patients by calling it a minor complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 不要把病人的疼痛说成小毛病，那等于轻描淡写。
senses.why: Talking is the main tool of the word: the same facts, described in little words, lose their weight, so the verb also names this way of speaking.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最主要的工具是语言：同样的事实一旦用小词来描述，重量就消失了，因此它又指这种说话方式本身。

senses.title: To oversimplify a complex problem
senses.definition: to strip a difficult or complicated problem down to a simple version, ignoring its real difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 把困难、复杂的问题剥成简单版本，忽略其真实难度
senses.example: The proposal trivializes the physics of keeping a man alive on Mars.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案把在火星上维持人生命的物理难题给简单化了。
senses.why: If everything at the crossroads is common, then hard matters can be cut into easy ones, and the word grows a second branch where complexity is erased.
senses.whyCN: 如果三岔路口的一切都平常，那么难事也能被切碎成易事，于是这个词长出第二个分支：复杂性被抹掉。

senses.title: To present an easy or trivial version
senses.titleCN: 删繁就简的版本；简化版演绎
senses.definition: to present a simplified or easy version of a work, theory, or practice
senses.definitionCN: 呈现作品、理论或做法的简化、容易版本
senses.example: The popular book trivializes the original research into a set of tips.
senses.exampleCN: 这本通俗读物把原先的研究简化成了一堆小贴士。
senses.why: Popular writing often takes serious work and serves it as a set of simple rules, and the verb marks exactly that shrink from depth to tips.
senses.whyCN: 通俗写作常把严肃的研究供应成一串简单规则，这个词恰好标记了从深度缩水成「小贴士」的过程。

senses.title: To treat a person with contempt
senses.definition: to regard a person or their concerns as beneath serious attention
senses.definitionCN: 认为某人或其关切不值得认真对待
senses.example: Her colleagues trivialized her worries until the report was filed.
senses.exampleCN: 同事们一直轻视她的担忧，直到报告正式提交。
senses.why: When a person becomes a crossroads figure, their voice loses weight, so the word extends from matters to people and their concerns.
senses.whyCN: 当一个人被当成街头的普通路人，其声音也就失去分量，于是这个词从「事」延伸到「人」与「人的关切」。

senses.title: To become trivial in effect
senses.titleCN: 变得无足轻重；沦为琐碎
senses.definition: to become or make a term or practice so common that it no longer carries weight
senses.definitionCN: 使术语或做法变得过于普遍，从而失去分量
senses.example: The word genius has been trivialized by advertising.
senses.exampleCN: 天才这个词已经被广告用得失去了分量。
senses.why: The passive form records a slow wearing down: once everyone uses a big word for anything, the word itself slips toward the crossroads meaning.
senses.whyCN: 被动形式记录了一种缓慢的磨损：当人人都拿大词来说任何事，这个词本身就滑向了「街头琐事」的含义。

senses.title: To deem a risk acceptable or minor
senses.titleCN: 把风险估得过低；认为风险微不足道
senses.definition: to judge a danger as too slight to act on
senses.definitionCN: 把危险判得过轻，因而不予处理
senses.example: Engineers who trivialize small cracks soon face structural failure.
senses.exampleCN: 把细小裂缝看得微不足道的工程师，很快就会遇到结构失效。
senses.why: The visual core is a heavy tower built from little stones; calling a crack a little stone is exactly this risk judgment.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是把沉重的塔拆成小石子；把一条裂缝称为一颗小石子，正是这种风险评估。

senses.title: To make a term too common to matter
senses.titleCN: 滥用成陈词滥调；使失去意义
senses.definition: to spread a word or idea so widely and loosely that it loses precise meaning
senses.definitionCN: 把一个词或观念用得过滥过泛，以致失去准确意义
senses.example: Media coverage trivializes grief by turning it into a stock phrase.
senses.exampleCN: 媒体报道把悲痛变成套话，等于让它失去意义。
senses.why: The same road metaphor eases the word into ordinary speech until the once weighty term becomes a stock phrase, the last stop of the semantic chain.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「道路」隐喻把词推入日常口语，直到原本沉重的术语变成套话，这是语义链的最后一站。

intro.en: Trivialize comes from the adjective trivial, from Latin trivium, the meeting of three roads, through the idea of things common to the street.
intro.cn: trivialize 来自形容词 trivial，上溯拉丁语 trivium（三条路交会之处），经由「街头巷尾的寻常事物」这一层意思演变而来。

items.en: Trivium means a place where three roads meet, from tri, three, and via, road.
items.cn: trivium 意为三条路交会之处，由 tri（三）与 via（路）构成。

items.en: Trivialis means belonging to the crossroads, hence common or ordinary.
items.cn: trivialis 意为属于路口街头的，因而解释为「普通的、日常的」。

items.en: The trivium names the first three liberal arts: grammar, logic, and rhetoric.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语里 trivium 指三艺：语法、逻辑与修辞。

items.en: A learned French form keeps the sense of common or ordinary.
items.cn: 法语中的学究式形式保留了「普通、平常」的含义。

items.en: The adjective trivial settles in English as trifling and unimportant.
items.cn: 形容词 trivial 在英语中定型为「琐碎的、不重要的」。

items.en: The verb trivialize appears in dictionaries of British English in the twentieth century, meaning to make trifling.
items.cn: 派生动词 trivialize 于二十世纪收入英国英语词典，义为「使变得琐碎」。

note.en: Trivialize is the verb built on trivial, standing at the crossroads where big matters are cut down to little ones.
note.cn: trivialize 是建立在 trivial 之上的动词，站在三岔路口：把大事切成小事。
