definition_zh: （演员、歌手等的）剧团；巡回演出团；一群表演者
definition_en: a group of actors, singers, dancers or other performers who work and travel together
core_image: 一辆装满戏服的马车停在村口，演员们一起卸下箱子上台
scene: 小镇广场上搭起临时戏台，马车旁挤满等候的观众。A travelling troupe arrived at dusk and performed under the lanterns.
sceneCN: 这里 troupe 是「巡回演出团」（第 3 个义项：巡回演出的表演团体）；句意为一个巡回剧团在黄昏到达，在灯笼下演出。

pos.zh: 名词：剧团；演出团；一群表演者

forms.label: 所属格（名词）
forms.form: troupe is used with of as in a troupe of dancers

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「剧团演员；老演员」
由动词加动名词词尾构成，义为「随团巡演」
与本词同源的双写体，义为「（一）群；部队」，是拼写相近而非派生

senses.title: A company of actors
senses.definition: a small company of actors who perform plays together, often outside permanent theatre buildings
senses.definitionCN: 一起演戏的小型演员班子，常在固定剧场之外演出
senses.example: The old troupe still performs Shakespeare every summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这个老剧团每年夏天仍演出莎士比亚的戏。
senses.why: Old French troupe meant a band or company, and actors borrowed it as the name of their working band.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 troupe 意为「一帮人、一群」，演员借用它来指一起干活的那一帮人。

senses.title: A dance or music group
senses.definition: a group of dancers, singers or circus performers who appear together as a unit
senses.definitionCN: 一起作为整体登台的舞者、歌手或马戏演员
senses.example: A young dance troupe opened the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 一个年轻的舞蹈团为艺术节开场。
senses.why: Once troupe meant a company of performers, other kinds of performers took the same word.
senses.whyCN: troupe 一旦指表演者班底，其他门类的表演者也顺势用同一个词。

senses.title: A travelling company
senses.definition: a company of performers that tours from town to town giving shows
senses.definitionCN: 从一个城镇巡回到另一个城镇演出的表演团体
senses.example: The travelling troupe spent a night in every village.
senses.exampleCN: 这支巡回剧团在每个村子住一夜。
senses.why: Troupes travelled because they had no permanent home stage, so travelling became part of the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 巡回剧团没有固定的主场舞台，只能四处演出，于是「巡演」成了词义的一部分。

senses.title: A band of companions
senses.definition: a group of people who move about together, used with a light or old-fashioned tone
senses.definitionCN: 一起行动的一群人，语气略带轻松或古旧色彩
senses.example: A happy troupe of students filled the train carriage.
senses.exampleCN: 一车欢快的学生挤满了车厢。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the word: simply a band or group, before actors made it their own.
senses.whyCN: 这是词最古老的一层含义：普通的「一帮人」，后来才被演员占为己有。

senses.title: The people rather than the building
senses.definition: the company of performers as distinct from the theatre building or its management
senses.definitionCN: 指演出的人员班底，区别于剧场建筑或管理层
senses.example: The town built the hall, but the troupe brought the plays.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上盖了礼堂，戏却是由剧团带来的。
senses.why: The loanword keeps the image of a band of people, so it names the performers where theatre names the place.
senses.whyCN: 这个借词始终带着「一群人」的意象，因此它指演的人，而 theatre 指演的地方。

senses.title: To travel as a company
senses.titleCN: 成群结队地走；随团巡演
senses.definition: to travel or move in a group, often as performers touring, chiefly in older or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 成群结队地行走或移动，多指演员随团巡演，多为较古旧或文学用法
senses.example: They trouped through the rain to the next town.
senses.exampleCN: 他们冒着雨赶往下一座城镇。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: to do what a troupe does, which is to move and perform as one band.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词：做剧团会做的事，即作为一个班子一起行动和演出。

intro.en: Troupe comes from Old French troupe, a band or company, which was borrowed into English. The root is usually traced to Frankish and further back to a Germanic word for a troop of soldiers.
intro.cn: troupe 来自古法语 troupe「一帮人、一群」，借入英语。词源一般认为可追到法兰克语，再往前是日耳曼语中表示「一队士兵」的词。

items.en: A reconstructed Frankish form such as *throp is generally proposed as the source of troupe; the exact shape is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: 一般认为 troupe 源于一个重构的法兰克语形式，如 *throp；确切形态属于重构而非文献记录。

items.en: Troupe meant a band, a company or a crowd of people moving together.
items.cn: troupe 意为「一帮人、一群、一起行动的一伙」，还不限于表演者。

items.en: English borrowed the word; its early uses are uncertain in detail, and it overlapped for a while with the doublet troop.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词；早期个别用法细节不确定，并且有一段时间与同源的 troop 难以区分。

items.en: Troupe came to be used mainly of companies of actors, dancers and other performers.
items.cn: troupe 逐渐主要用于指演员、舞者等表演者的班子。

items.en: The spelling now marks the performer sense, while troop keeps the military and general crowd senses.
items.cn: 今天的拼写形式专门标示「表演团体」，而 troop 保留军事与一般人群的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same group word in its various spellings and derived forms; the near-meaning group names other kinds of companies and companies of players.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个「一群人」之词的不同拼写与派生形式；近义组收其他类型的团社与班底。

entries.definition: A group of soldiers, or a group of people or animals; the same word in its older spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 指一队士兵，或一群人和动物；与本词同源，属较早的拼写形式。

entries.definition: A member of a company of performers, especially one who has long experience.
entries.definitionCN: 剧团的成员，尤指经验丰富的老演员；由本词加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The act of touring as a company of performers.
entries.definitionCN: 随团巡演的行为；由本词的动词形式加动名词词尾构成。

entries.definition: A group of actors working together; the standard word that troupe echoes.
entries.definitionCN: 一起工作的演员团体；troupe 呼应的那类标准说法。

entries.definition: All the actors chosen for one particular play, film or show.
entries.definitionCN: 为某一部戏、影片或节目选定的全部演员。

entries.definition: A group of musicians, or more generally any small group joined by a common aim.
entries.definitionCN: 音乐团体，也可泛指因共同目标而结合的小群体。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French source, the spelling contrast with troop, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子用真实的法语来源、与 troop 的拼写差别，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Troupe is the French spelling of troop: same word, but here the group is actors, not soldiers.
normal.cn: troupe 是 troop 的法语式拼写：同一个词，只是这里的一群人是演员，不是士兵。

normal.en: A trouper is one member of the troupe; the -er ending marks the person.
normal.cn: trouper 是剧团里的一个人；词尾 -er 标示「人」。

normal.en: A theatre troupe, a dance troupe and a travelling troupe all name the same kind of working band.
normal.cn: theatre troupe、dance troupe 与 travelling troupe 指的都是同一类工作班底。

normal.en: Compare company: company is the general word, troupe is the livelier and slightly old-fashioned one.
normal.cn: 对比 company：company 是一般说法，troupe 更生动，也略带古旧色彩。

normal.en: The verb to troupe keeps the image of moving as a band from town to town.
normal.cn: 动词 to troupe 保留了「整队从一个城镇走到另一个城镇」的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a painted wagon with wooden trunks tied on top, pulling up where a crowd is already waiting.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆画着图案的马车，车顶捆着木箱，停下的地方已经围满了等戏的人。

abstract.en: Imagine five actors bowing in one line, then packing the same five costumes back into one crate.
abstract.cn: 想象五个演员排成一排鞠躬，然后把同样的五套戏服重新装回一只木箱。

abstract.en: Think of a village square after dark: a lantern, a rope stage, and people who came in one cart and will leave in it.
abstract.cn: 想象入夜后的村口广场：一盏灯笼、一处绳围的舞台，一群人同乘一辆车来，也将同乘这辆车走。

examples.en: A theatre troupe from the capital visited the school.
examples.cn: 一支来自首都的剧团访问了这所学校。

examples.en: The dance troupe rehearsed until midnight.
examples.cn: 舞蹈团排练到午夜。

examples.en: She toured with a small troupe for three years.
examples.cn: 她随一个小剧团巡演了三年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吐露」——剧团一上台就向观众吐露心声；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 troupe「一帮人、一群」，一般认为源自法兰克语重构形式 *throp，更早可追到日耳曼语表示「一队兵」的词；与英语 troop 同源，仅仅是拼写分化。早期借入英语的确切年代与用法存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Troupe starts as a plain band of people, narrows to actors and then to dancers and singers, keeps its life on the road, survives as a light word for any group of companions, marks performers rather than buildings, and finally becomes a verb of travelling in a band.
sensesIntro.cn: troupe 最初只是「一帮人」，收窄为演员班组，再扩到舞者与歌手，保留「在路上」的身份，作为轻松说法泛指同伴群体，标示演的人而非演的场所，最后转为「整队四处走」的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one wagon arrives at a village square and unloads a whole company of players.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆马车驶进村口广场，卸下一整班子演戏的人。

branches.en: The actor line: a working band of players is the word at its centre.
branches.cn: 演员线：一班子演戏的人是这个词的核心。

branches.en: The wider performer line: dancers, singers and circus artists join the same band.
branches.cn: 表演者扩展线：舞者、歌手与马戏演员也走进同一个班子。

branches.en: The road line: moving from town to town turns the group into a touring company and then into a verb.
branches.cn: 路上线：从一个城镇走到另一个城镇，把团体变成演出团，再变成动词。

branches.en: The old general line: any group of companions still carries the earliest meaning.
branches.cn: 古老一般义：任何一群同伴都还带着最早的那层意思。

branches.en: The contrast line: performers rather than the theatre that houses them.
branches.cn: 对照线：指的是演的人，而不是收留他们的戏院。

intro.en: Troupe is a French loanword with almost no internal structure: the whole borrowed noun carries the meaning, and English adds only the agent -er and the verbal endings.
intro.cn: troupe 是几乎没有内部结构的法语借词：整个借来的名词承载词义，英语只添上表示「人」的 -er 和动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Troupe does not come from Latin; it is usually traced to Frankish through Old French. The Latin list is therefore empty except for the later French forms that English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: troupe 并非来自拉丁语，一般认为经由古法语上溯至法兰克语。因此这里的拉丁语部分为空，只保留英语后来借入的法语形式。

items.meaning: a band, a company of people
items.example: The French noun is the whole borrowed body of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语名词就是整个借来的词身。

items.example: The English noun narrows the band to performers.
items.exampleCN: 英语名词把「一群人」收窄为表演者。

items.example: The suffix -er forms trouper from troupe.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 把 troupe 变成 trouper。

items.meaning: a long-serving actor in a company
items.example: A trouper stays on when others leave the road.
items.exampleCN: 别人离开巡演路线时，trouper 仍然留下。

items.example: The ending -ing forms trouping.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 trouping。

items.example: Plural troupes marks several performing companies.
items.exampleCN: 复数 troupes 指多个演出团体。

items.example: Troop keeps the older spelling of the same band.
items.exampleCN: troop 保留同一个词的较早拼写。

items.example: The verb troop shares the trouping image.
items.exampleCN: 动词 troop 与「整队行进」的画面相通。

items.example: Trooping describes the movement of the band.
items.exampleCN: trooping 描述这个班子一起行动。

items.example: The later military sense fixed troop on soldiers.
items.exampleCN: 后来才固化的军事义把 troop 定给了士兵。

definition_zh: 逃学的（学生）；旷课的；无所事事、游荡的
definition_en: staying away from school or work without permission, or wandering about instead of doing what one should
core_image: 课堂上少了一张椅子，那孩子正隔着街头看窗外
scene: 上课铃响过，后排靠窗的座位却一直空着，书包还挂在椅背上。The teacher marked him as truant and sent a note to his parents.
sceneCN: 这里 truant 是「逃学的」（第 1 个义项：该到校却无故缺席）；句意为老师把他记为逃学并通知了家长。

pos.zh: 形容词：逃学的；旷课的；游荡的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词词尾 -cy 构成，义为「逃学；旷课」
由本词加副词词尾 -ly 构成，义为「逃学地；懒散地」
由动词加动名词词尾构成，义为「逃学行为」

senses.title: Missing school without permission
senses.definition: a pupil who stays away from school without permission or a good reason
senses.definitionCN: 未经允许或无正当理由不到校的学生
senses.example: The truant boy spent the morning by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 那个逃学的男孩在河边待了一上午。
senses.why: Old French truant meant a vagrant or beggar, so a child who says he is at school but is not is a wanderer in the eyes of the school.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 truant 意为「流浪者、乞丐」，因此学校眼里那个「说去上学却没去」的孩子就是游荡的人。

senses.title: Absent from a duty
senses.titleCN: 失职不到的；无故缺席的
senses.definition: failing to appear for a duty, a meeting or a task when expected
senses.definitionCN: 在规定应当到场时没有出现，如缺席职责、会议或任务
senses.example: Three truant members were asked to explain their absence.
senses.exampleCN: 三名无故缺席的成员被要求说明原因。
senses.why: The school sense widened: any duty can be skipped the way a lesson is skipped.
senses.whyCN: 逃学义被放宽：任何职责都可以像一节课那样被跳过去。

senses.title: Idle and wandering
senses.definition: idle, lazy, or given to wandering about instead of doing proper work
senses.definitionCN: 懒散、游荡，该干活却不干活
senses.example: The truant afternoon slipped past with nothing done.
senses.exampleCN: 那个懒散的下午一事无成地过去了。
senses.why: The earliest French meaning was vagrancy, so idleness and wandering remain the deepest layer of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早的法语含义就是「流浪」，因此懒散与游荡始终是它最深的一层意思。

senses.title: Playing truant from school
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase play truant or play truant from school, to stay away from school deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 在固定短语 play truant 或 play truant from school 中，指故意不去学校
senses.example: The children played truant to watch the fair.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们逃学去看集市。
senses.why: The verb play turns the noun into an activity: one plays at being absent as one plays at being elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 动词 play 把这个名词变成一种活动：把缺席当作一场游戏来过。

senses.title: The truant officer
senses.definition: in compounds such as truant officer, an official whose work concerns pupils who miss school
senses.definitionCN: 在 truant officer 等复合词中，指负责处理学生缺席问题的官员
senses.example: The truant officer called at the house twice.
senses.exampleCN: 督学两次上门家访。
senses.why: When school attendance became law, the wandering child needed a name and an official to chase the name.
senses.whyCN: 当上学成为法律义务之后，那个游荡的孩子需要一个称呼，也需要一位官员来追赶这个称呼。

senses.title: To stay away from school
senses.definition: to stay away from school or from work without permission, used in British and older register
senses.definitionCN: 未经许可不到校或不上工，多用于英式英语和较旧语域
senses.example: He truanted from school three times that term.
senses.exampleCN: 那个学期他逃了三次学。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: the child does the truant thing rather than being called a truant.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词：孩子是在做「逃学」这件事，而不再只是被叫作逃学者。

intro.en: Truant comes from Old French truant, a wandering beggar or vagabond, which English borrowed. The deeper origin of the French word is disputed rather than agreed.
intro.cn: truant 来自古法语 truant，指四处流浪的乞丐或流浪汉，被英语借入。这个法语词更深层的来源有争议，并无定论。

items.en: Truant named a vagabond, a beggar or an idle rogue; the connection with the modern word is clear.
items.cn: truant 指流浪汉、乞丐或游手好闲的浪荡子；与现代含义的联系是明确的。

items.en: Several explanations have been offered: from a Celtic word for a wretch, from Latin trudere, to push, or as a formation from Gaulish elements. None is generally accepted.
items.cn: 来源不确定：有说法认为来自凯尔特语表示「可怜人」的词，或来自拉丁语 trudere「推」，或由高卢语成分构成；各家均未获得公认。

items.en: English records truant first in the senses of vagrant and idle person; the exact first quotation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语约在公元一千三百年记录到 truant，最初是「流浪者」和「懒汉」义；确切的首见引文不确定。

items.en: Truant became the standard word for a pupil who stays away from school, and play truant fixed the phrase.
items.cn: truant 成为指逃学学生的标准用词，play truant 也固定下来。

items.en: The abstract noun truancy and compounds such as truant officer came to serve schooling law and child welfare.
items.cn: 抽象名词 truancy 与 truant officer 一类复合词开始服务于义务教育和儿童福利事务。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same wanderer family and the forms built on it; the near-meaning group gathers other names for the child who is not in class.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「游荡者」词族及其派生形式；近义组收其他指「不在教室里的孩子」的说法。

entries.definition: The act or habit of staying away from school without permission.
entries.definitionCN: 未经许可不到校的行为或习惯；由本词加 -cy 构成。

entries.definition: In an idle or wandering manner; a rare adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 以懒散或游荡的方式；罕见副词，由本词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The act of staying away from school, used as a noun or participle.
entries.definitionCN: 逃学行为；作名词或分词使用。

entries.definition: A person who is not present when expected, often a pupil who is often away.
entries.definitionCN: 本该在场却缺席的人，常指经常缺课的学生。

entries.definition: A pupil who leaves school before finishing; longer-lasting than truancy.
entries.definitionCN: 中途辍学者；比逃学更持久，指离开学校不再回来。

entries.definition: A person without a settled home who wanders; the old meaning behind truant.
entries.definitionCN: 无固定居所、四处流浪的人；正是 truant 的古老含义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French source truant, its vagrant past, and the phrases and derivatives the word actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的法语来源 truant、它「流浪者」的旧义，以及这个词实际构成的搭配与派生词。

normal.en: Truant once meant a wanderer, so a truant child is one who wandered away from the classroom.
normal.cn: truant 原本指流浪者，因此逃学的孩子就是从教室里游荡出去的那个人。

normal.en: Play truant is the fixed phrase; play marks the skipping of school as an act.
normal.cn: play truant 是固定搭配；play 把「逃课」标成一个动作。

normal.en: Truancy is the abstract noun: the school records truancy, a teacher marks one pupil as a truant.
normal.cn: truancy 是抽象名词：学校记录的是逃学行为，老师标记的是某个逃学者。

normal.en: Compare absent: a pupil can be absent with permission, but a truant is absent without one.
normal.cn: 对比 absent：学生可以请假缺席，而 truant 是无故缺席。

normal.en: Truant officer shows how the word entered the machinery of compulsory schooling.
normal.cn: truant officer 显示这个词是怎样进入义务教育管理体系的。

abstract.en: Picture a classroom with one empty chair near the window and a backpack still hooked on it.
abstract.cn: 想象教室靠窗的位置空着一把椅子，书包还挂在椅背上。

abstract.en: Follow the boy in the picture: he walks away from the school gate, slowly, with the schoolbag bouncing at his side and no plan at all.
abstract.cn: 跟着画面中那个孩子看：他慢慢离开校门，书包在身边一颠一颠，全然没有计划。

abstract.en: Look at the empty chair from the teacher side: the question is not who is late, but who should be there and is not.
abstract.cn: 从老师一侧看那把空椅子：问题不是谁迟到，而是谁本该在场却不在。

examples.en: The truant pupil was found at the arcade after lunch.
examples.cn: 那个逃学的学生午饭后被发现在游戏厅。

examples.en: Schools now report truancy rates every term.
examples.cn: 学校如今每学期报告旷课率。

examples.en: He was marked as truant for three mornings running.
examples.cn: 他连续三个早晨被记为旷课。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「出安」——不去上学，溜出校门图个心安；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 truant「流浪汉；乞丐；懒汉」，约自一千三百年起进入英语；其更深来源有争议，一般认为可能来自凯尔特语表示「可怜人」的词，或与拉丁语 trudere「推」有关，均未获公认。

sensesIntro.en: Truant travels from a wandering beggar to a pupil absent from school, then widens to any absent duty, keeps the old idleness of the wanderer, lives inside the phrase play truant, becomes the short form in compounds such as truant officer, and finally turns into a verb of skipping school.
sensesIntro.cn: truant 从四处流浪的乞丐走到缺课的学生，再扩展到任何失职不到的场合，保留流浪者古老的懒散义，活在 play truant 短语里，成为 truant officer 一类复合词中的成分，最后转为「逃课」的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one chair in the classroom is empty, and the pupil who should fill it is wandering outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：教室里空着一把椅子，原本该坐上去的学生正在外面游荡。

branches.en: The school line: the wanderer becomes the pupil who is not in class.
branches.cn: 学校线：流浪者变成了不在教室里的那个学生。

branches.en: The widened duty line: any expected presence can be skipped.
branches.cn: 职责扩展线：任何本应到场的场合都可能被跳过。

branches.en: The old character line: idleness is the earliest French meaning kept under the surface.
branches.cn: 性格旧义线：懒散是法语最早的含义，藏在表层之下。

branches.en: The institution line: a fixed phrase and a compound office grew around compulsory schooling.
branches.cn: 制度线：固定短语与专设官职都围绕义务教育生长出来。

branches.en: The action line: the noun becomes a verb, and the child skips rather than merely is absent.
branches.cn: 动作线：名词变成动词，孩子是主动「逃」，而不只是「缺」。

intro.en: Truant is a French loanword with little internal structure; English only adds noun, adverb and verbal endings to extend it.
intro.cn: truant 是内部结构不多的法语借词；英语只添上名词、副词与动词词尾来扩展它。

latinIntro.en: Truant is usually taken as French or Frankish in origin, not Latin. One proposal links it to Latin trudere, to push, but this is not settled, so the Latin list stays short.
latinIntro.cn: truant 通常被认为源自法语或法兰克语，而非拉丁语。有一种说法把它与拉丁语 trudere「推」联系起来，但尚无定论，因此拉丁语部分从简。

items.example: The French word contributes the whole body of the term.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语词提供整个词身。

items.example: The English noun narrows the vagrant to a pupil.
items.exampleCN: 英语名词把「流浪者」收窄为「学生」。

items.example: The suffix -cy forms truancy from truant.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -cy 把 truant 变成 truancy。

items.example: Truancy names the habit, not the person.
items.exampleCN: truancy 指习惯，不指人。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms truantly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 truantly。

items.example: The ending -ant marks the doer in truant.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 在 truant 中标示「做事的人」。

items.example: The phrase keeps the noun inside a verb of play.
items.exampleCN: 这一短语把名词嵌进了 play 这一动词。

items.example: The ending -ing forms truanting.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 truanting。

items.meaning: an official dealing with absentee pupils
items.meaningCN: 处理学生缺席事务的官员
items.example: The compound anchors truant in school law.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把 truant 固定在教育法规中。

definition_zh: 停战；休战；停战协定；暂时的停歇
definition_en: an agreement between enemies to stop fighting for a limited time, or a short pause in any dispute
core_image: 两军中间插下一面白旗，枪口同时垂下来
scene: 边境的两个村子打了半年，长老们终于坐下来约定先放下武器。The two villages along the border at last agreed to a truce and laid down their weapons.
sceneCN: 这里 truce 是「停战、休战」（第 1 个义项：敌对双方约定期限内停止交战）；句意：边境的两个村子终于商定了停战，放下了武器。

collocations.phrase: a truce between A and B

derivatives.zh: 由 truce 加形容词后缀 -ial 构成，义为「停战协定的；休战的」，多见于海湾地名
truce 加 breaker（破坏者）构成的复合词，义为「破坏停战者」
truce 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「不肯停战的、没有休战的」

senses.title: A formal halt to fighting
senses.definition: an agreement between opposing sides to stop fighting for a stated or limited period
senses.definitionCN: 敌对双方约定在确定或有限的时间内停止交战的协议
senses.example: The two generals signed a truce that would last for one week.
senses.exampleCN: 两位将军签署了为期一周的停战协议。
senses.why: The oldest meaning is an agreement for a set term, so the core image is a flag put down between two armies.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是约定期限的协议，所以核心意象是两面军阵之间插下一面白旗。

senses.title: A breathing space in a quarrel
senses.definition: a short break in an argument or in any ongoing dispute short of war
senses.definitionCN: 争论尚未升级为战争时的短暂缓冲或停顿
senses.example: The family agreed to a truce over dinner and talked about the weather.
senses.exampleCN: 一家人约定晚饭时先休战，只谈天气。
senses.why: Because a truce never means peace itself, it easily moves from battlefields to quarrels that just need a pause.
senses.whyCN: 停战本身从不等于和平，于是这个词很自然地由战场移用到只需要缓一缓的日常争执。

senses.title: A pause in a hard struggle
senses.definition: a temporary relief from any intense activity or pressure, such as work or competition
senses.definitionCN: 在工作、竞争等强烈活动或压力中得到的暂时缓解
senses.example: Newcomers called a truce in the price war by matching the leader.
senses.exampleCN: 新入局者追随领头羊的价格，让这场价格战暂时停了下来。
senses.why: Any contest can be imagined as a battlefield, so the pause it brings borrows the truce word.
senses.whyCN: 任何竞争都能被想象成战场，所以竞争中的停顿也借用了停战这个词。

intro.en: Truce comes from Old English treow, a pledge of faith or an agreement, reinforced by the related Middle English form triwe and the verb treowian, to trust.
intro.cn: truce 来自古英语 treow（信义、契约），与中古英语的 triwe、动词 treowian（信任）同出一源。

items.en: The reconstructed root treuwaz gives the idea of good faith and loyalty.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构形式 treuwaz 表示「信义、忠诚」。

items.en: Treow means a promise, faith, or covenant, and treowian means to trust.
items.cn: 古英语 treow 意为承诺、信义、契约，treowian 意为信任。

items.en: The northern form triwe and related spellings drift towards the sense of a pledge to stop war.
items.cn: 中古英语北部的 triwe 等写法逐渐转向「停战承诺」这一含义。

items.en: Trewes or truwes are recorded in the sense of an agreement to stop fighting.
items.cn: trewes、truwes 等记录开始表示「停止交战的协议」。

items.en: The final -w disappears and truce settles as the ordinary spelling.
items.cn: 词尾的 w 消失，拼写固定为 truce。

items.en: The military sense stays, and the word spreads to arguments, rivalries, and everyday life.
items.cn: 军事义保留下来，又扩散到争论、竞争与日常生活。

note.en: Truce belongs to the faith and pledge family, so its look-alikes come from Old English treow, while its near meanings are words for stopping a fight.
note.cn: truce 属于「信义、承诺」词族，形近词多出自古英语 treow；近义一侧则是表达「停止交战」的词。

entries.definition: in accordance with fact or reality
entries.definitionCN: 真实的；与事实相符的（与 truce 同出于古英语「信义」词根）

entries.definition: the quality of being in accordance with fact
entries.definitionCN: 真相；真实性（同根名词）

entries.definition: in a genuine or sincere way
entries.definitionCN: 真正地；真诚地

entries.definition: firm belief in the reliability of someone
entries.definitionCN: 信任；信赖（与 truce 同源，都建立在信义之上）

entries.definition: an order or agreement to stop firing weapons
entries.definitionCN: 停火；停火令（比 truce 更强调真正停止开火）

entries.definition: a formal agreement to end fighting in a war
entries.definitionCN: 停战协定；休战（正式，常指结束整场战争）

entries.definition: a state with no war or conflict
entries.definitionCN: 和平；和睦（停战只是走向和平的一步）

normalIntro.en: Truce grew out of the old word for faith and a pledge, so a truce is a promise sworn between enemies.
normalIntro.cn: truce 由表示信义与承诺的古老词演化而来，所以停战就是敌对双方之间立下的誓约。

normal.en: To call a truce is to ask both sides to stop fighting for a while.
normal.cn: call a truce 就是请双方暂时停止交战。

normal.en: Anyone who breaks the truce is seen as breaking a promise.
normal.cn: 破坏停战协定的人，等于背弃了承诺，这正是词源里「信义」的延伸。

normal.en: Compare true and trust: all three share the old sense of being faithful.
normal.cn: 对比 true 与 trust：这三个词共享「忠实」这一古老含义。

normal.en: A truce is always temporary, while peace is meant to be lasting.
normal.cn: truce 总是临时的，而 peace 意在长久。

normal.en: We often call a truce in an argument when we simply want to change the subject.
normal.cn: 我们常在争论中宣布休战，其实只是想换个话题。

abstract.en: Picture a white flag rising slowly between two lines of soldiers.
abstract.cn: 想象一面白旗在两排士兵之间缓缓升起。

abstract.en: Think of two neighbours stopping their shouting to share a meal.
abstract.cn: 想象两位邻居停止吵嚷，坐下来一起吃饭。

abstract.en: Imagine a referee blowing the whistle so both teams can catch their breath.
abstract.cn: 想象裁判吹响哨子，让两支球队都喘口气。

examples.en: The rebels and the government reached a truce after months of fighting.
examples.cn: 叛军与政府在数月交战之后达成了停战。

examples.en: Let us call a truce and talk about this calmly.
examples.cn: 我们先休战，冷静地谈一谈吧。

examples.en: The truce held for only three days before the shelling began again.
examples.cn: 停战只维持了三天，炮击就又开始了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特鲁斯」——两队人马喊一句「特鲁斯」就都收枪停火；记 truce 是停战。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 treow（信义、契约、忠诚）+ treowian（信任）→ 中古英语 triwe、trewes（停战承诺）→ 词尾 w 消失，成为 truce，核心义「以信义立约，暂停交战」。

sensesIntro.en: Truce starts as a sworn pledge between armies, then widens to a pause in a quarrel and finally to any relief from intense struggle.
sensesIntro.cn: truce 起初是军队之间立誓的约定，随后扩展到争执中的暂停，最后泛指激烈角逐中的喘息。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white flag planted between two armies.
core.cn: 核心意象：两面军阵之间插下的一面白旗。

branches.en: The sworn, time-limited halt in battle is the original sense.
branches.cn: 立誓且有时限的停止交战，是这个词最原始的义项。

branches.en: A pause in an argument borrows the flag image from the battlefield.
branches.cn: 争执中的暂停，把战场的白旗意象借到了日常。

branches.en: Any intense competition can be pictured as a front line that falls quiet.
branches.cn: 任何激烈竞争都可以想象成一条暂时安静下来的战线。

branches.en: Both a limited halt and a dinner pause are temporary by design.
branches.cn: 有时限的停战和饭桌休战，本质上都是刻意的暂时安排。

branches.en: An armistice and a price war truce both rely on promises holding on both sides.
branches.cn: 战场休战与价格战休战，都依赖双方共同遵守承诺。

intro.en: Truce is a whole word from Old English rather than a built form, and it sits in a family with true, truth, trust, and the rare adjective trucial.
intro.cn: truce 是完整的古英语词，而非拼装而成；它与 true、truth、trust 以及少见的形容词 trucial 同属一个词族。

latinIntro.en: Truce has no Latin source, since it comes from the Germanic word for faith; its look-alikes are English kin rather than borrowed Latin forms.
latinIntro.cn: truce 并无拉丁语来源，它出自日耳曼语中表示信义的词；相关词都是英语同族词，而不是借入的拉丁词形。

items.example: Treow supplies the pledge meaning.
items.exampleCN: treow 提供了「承诺」这一含义。

items.example: Truwe appears in northern records.
items.exampleCN: truwe 见于北部文献。

items.example: Truce is the modern spelling.
items.exampleCN: truce 是现代拼写形式。

items.example: The ending -s forms truces.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 truces。

items.example: The suffix -ial forms trucial.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ial 构成 trucial。

items.example: Trucial states were bound by truces.
items.exampleCN: 特鲁西尔诸邦由停战协定相互约束。

items.example: The combining form -breaker forms trucebreaker.
items.exampleCN: 组合成分 -breaker 构成 trucebreaker。

items.example: The suffix -less forms truceless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 truceless。

items.example: Truth shares the faith root of truce.
items.exampleCN: truth 与 truce 共享「信义」词根。

items.example: Trust grew from the same pledge idea.
items.exampleCN: trust 源自同一个「立约」概念。

definition_zh: 结核病；肺结核
definition_en: a serious infectious disease that mainly attacks the lungs and is caused by a bacterium
core_image: 布满小疙瘩的肺：每个结节像一颗埋在组织里的小瘤子
scene: 老照片里，病人躺在通风的疗养院阳台上，每天晒足太阳、吃足营养。Before modern drugs, patients with tuberculosis were sent to quiet mountain sanatoriums for fresh air and rest.
sceneCN: 这里 tuberculosis 是「肺结核」（第 1 个义项：由结核杆菌引起的传染病，最常侵犯肺部）；句意：在现代药物出现之前，肺结核病人会被送到安静的山地疗养院，靠新鲜空气和休息养病。

derivatives.zh: 由 tuberculosis 去尾部加形容词后缀 -ous 构成，义为「结核性的」
tuberculum 加形容词后缀 -ar 构成，义为「结核的；结核性的」
tuberculum 加表示物质的 -in 构成，义为「结核菌素」，用于皮试
前缀 anti-（抗）加 tuberculous 构成，义为「抗结核的」

senses.title: The infectious lung disease
senses.definition: a serious bacterial infection that most often damages the lungs and spreads through the air
senses.definitionCN: 一种严重的细菌感染，最常损害肺部，并通过空气传播
senses.example: The clinic screens every child for tuberculosis.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所为每个孩子做结核病筛查。
senses.why: The word was coined from the little lumps, called tubercles, that the disease leaves in tissue, so the image is the knobbly lung.
senses.whyCN: 这个词造自病灶组织中的「小结节」tubercle，所以意象就是布满疙瘩的肺。

senses.title: The bacterium behind it
senses.definition: used informally for the bacterium that causes the disease
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用来指引起该病的细菌本身
senses.example: Lab tests confirmed tuberculosis in the sputum sample.
senses.exampleCN: 化验确认痰样中有结核菌。
senses.why: Medical usage often names a disease by its cause, so the disease word slides onto the germ.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法常以病因代称疾病，于是这个病名滑移到了病菌身上。

senses.title: A knotted growth in tissue
senses.definition: an older medical use for any small round swelling or nodule in the body
senses.definitionCN: 旧时医学用法，泛指身体里小的圆形肿块或结节
senses.example: Early writers used tuberculosis for any tubercles in the tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 早期作者用 tuberculosis 泛指组织中的任何结节。
senses.why: Before the germ was found, the word simply described the knobbly shapes doctors saw, not a single disease.
senses.whyCN: 在发现病菌之前，这个词只是描述医生看到的疙瘩形状，而不是某一种病。

intro.en: Tuberculosis is a learned Latin coinage made from tuberculum, a little swelling, which is the diminutive of Latin tuber, a lump or growth.
intro.cn: tuberculosis 是学术性的拉丁语新造词，来自 tuberculum（小结节），而 tuberculum 是拉丁语 tuber（肿块、疙瘩）的指小形式。

items.en: Tuber means a swelling, lump, or growth, and also names the truffle.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tuber 意为肿块、疙瘩，也用来指块菌。

items.en: The diminutive tuberculum names a small nodule in the body.
items.cn: 指小形式 tuberculum 指身体里的小结节。

items.en: Physicians borrow tuberculum for little lumps seen in diseased organs.
items.cn: 十七世纪医生借 tuberculum 描述患病器官中的小结节。

items.en: Tuberculosis is formed with the Greek ending -osis, meaning a condition, and at first names nodules rather than one disease.
items.cn: 十九世纪用希腊语词尾 -osis（表示状态）造出 tuberculosis，最初指结节而非某一种病。

items.en: After the tubercle bacillus is identified in 1882, the word narrows to the disease of the lungs.
items.cn: 1882 年发现结核杆菌之后，该词收窄为肺结核这一疾病。

items.en: Modern medicine keeps tuberculosis as the official name and uses TB in daily speech.
items.cn: 现代医学以 tuberculosis 为正式病名，日常口语则用缩写 TB。

note.en: Tuberculosis belongs to the Latin lump and nodule family, and its near meanings are other names for serious lung and infectious disease.
note.cn: tuberculosis 属于拉丁语「肿块、结节」词族；近义一侧则是肺病与传染病领域的其他名称。

entries.definition: a small rounded swelling, especially in the lung
entries.definitionCN: 小结节；结核结节（词源核心，也就是词里的那串疙瘩）

entries.definition: relating to or caused by tuberculosis
entries.definitionCN: 结核性的；结核病引起的

entries.definition: a rounded underground stem such as a potato
entries.definitionCN: 块茎（如马铃薯），正是「肿块」的原始形象

entries.definition: a substance used in a skin test for tuberculosis
entries.definitionCN: 结核菌素，用于皮肤试验

entries.definition: the old name for tuberculosis of the lungs
entries.definitionCN: 肺结核的旧称，因病人日渐消瘦而得名

entries.definition: a wasting away of the body, especially from lung disease
entries.definitionCN: 肺痨；消瘦性病变，旧时的医学术语

entries.definition: an infection that inflames the lungs
entries.definitionCN: 肺炎（同为肺部感染，但病原与病程不同）

normalIntro.en: Tuberculosis carries its picture inside the word: tuber is a lump, and tuberculosis is the disease of lumps in the lung.
normalIntro.cn: tuberculosis 把画面写进了词里：tuber 是疙瘩，这个病就是肺里长满疙瘩的疾病。

normal.en: Contract tuberculosis means catching the disease, not signing a contract.
normal.cn: contract tuberculosis 是染上结核病，而不是签合同。

normal.en: TB is the everyday short form that doctors, patients, and news reports all use.
normal.cn: TB 是日常使用的缩写，医生、病人和新闻都用它。

normal.en: The -osis ending marks a medical condition, as it does in many disease names.
normal.cn: 词尾 -osis 在医学中标记某种状态，许多疾病名称都用它。

normal.en: Pulmonary comes from the Latin word for lungs, so pulmonary tuberculosis simply names the place attacked.
normal.cn: pulmonary 出自拉丁语「肺」，所以 pulmonary tuberculosis 就是点明受侵犯的部位。

normal.en: Compare consumption, the older word for the same disease that describes how a patient wastes away.
normal.cn: 对比 consumption：它是同一种病的旧称，描写的则是病人日渐消瘦的样子。

abstract.en: Picture a lung seen from above, dotted with tiny grey beads.
abstract.cn: 想象从上往下看一片肺，上面缀满灰色的小珠子。

abstract.en: Think of a row of small lumps you can feel under the skin.
abstract.cn: 想象皮下能摸到一排小疙瘩。

abstract.en: Imagine an old fashioned lamp shaped like a rounded lump.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏圆鼓鼓的旧式油灯，形状就像块茎。

examples.en: Tuberculosis remains one of the deadliest infectious diseases in the world.
examples.cn: 结核病仍是世界上最致命的传染病之一。

examples.en: The young nurse was vaccinated against tuberculosis before starting work.
examples.cn: 那位年轻护士上岗前接种了结核病疫苗。

examples.en: Doctors warn that tuberculosis can stay hidden for years before symptoms appear.
examples.cn: 医生提醒，结核病可能在症状出现前多年隐匿不显。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「丘伯克罗西斯」——想象山坡「丘」上长满疙瘩的草皮，像肺里的结核结节；记 tuberculosis 是结核病。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tuber（肿块、疙瘩）→ 指小形式 tuberculum（小结节）→ 医学拉丁语 tuberculosis（以希腊词尾 -osis 构成，指结节病）→ 英语 tuberculosis，核心义「组织里长满小结节的病」。

sensesIntro.en: Tuberculosis moves from the official name of the lung disease to the germ in casual talk, while the oldest use simply names nodules in the body.
sensesIntro.cn: tuberculosis 从肺病的正式名称，到口语里指病菌，再到古老的「结节」义项，一路都围绕组织里的小疙瘩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lung dotted with small hard lumps.
core.cn: 核心意象：布满小结节的肺。

branches.en: The nodule-making lung infection is the modern medical sense.
branches.cn: 以结节为特征的肺部感染，是现代医学主义项。

branches.en: Naming the germ is a loose everyday extension of the disease name.
branches.cn: 用病名称呼病菌，是口语对病名的一种松散延伸。

branches.en: The oldest use describes any nodule, before the germ was known.
branches.cn: 最古老的义项只是描述结节，当时还不知道有致病菌。

branches.en: Both the disease and the nodule point back to the same lump image.
branches.cn: 疾病与结节两个义项，都回到同一个「肿块」意象。

branches.en: The disease and its cause travel through the air together.
branches.cn: 疾病与致病菌都随空气一同传播。

intro.en: Tuberculosis is a modern scientific build: a Latin stem for lump, a diminutive suffix, and a Greek ending for a medical condition.
intro.cn: tuberculosis 是现代科学的拼装词：表示疙瘩的拉丁词干、指小后缀，加上表示病态的希腊词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin tuber is the lump itself, and the diminutive tuberculum is the small nodule that doctors felt in the diseased lung.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tuber 就是肿块本身，指小形式 tuberculum 则是医生在病肺里摸到的小结节。

items.example: Tuber is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: tuber 是整个词族的基座。

items.example: The suffix -culum makes tuberculum.
items.exampleCN: 指小词尾 -culum 构成 tuberculum。

items.example: Tuberculum appears in early anatomy texts.
items.exampleCN: tuberculum 见于早期解剖学文献。

items.example: The suffix -osis marks a medical condition.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -osis 标记医学状态。

items.example: Tuberculosis is the scholarly coinage.
items.exampleCN: tuberculosis 是学术造词。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms tuberculous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 构成 tuberculous。

items.example: Tuberculous describes tissue damage.
items.exampleCN: tuberculous 描述结核性损伤。

items.example: The suffix -in forms tuberculin.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -in 构成 tuberculin。

items.example: The prefix anti- forms antituberculous.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 anti- 构成 antituberculous。

items.meaning: a rounded stem of a potato
items.meaningCN: 块茎；马铃薯那样圆鼓鼓的茎
items.example: Tuber appears in everyday gardening words.
items.exampleCN: tuber 也出现在日常园艺用语中。

definition_zh: 用力拉；猛拽；拖船；一股强烈的感情
definition_en: to pull something hard and suddenly, or a strong pull, or a small powerful boat that pulls larger ships
core_image: 两只手死死攥住绳子，身子后倾，一寸一寸把东西拖过来
scene: 爸爸想把绳子从孩子手里拿走，孩子却抓紧不放，两人来回拉扯。The little girl tugged at her fathers sleeve, eager to show him the new puppy.
sceneCN: 这里 tug 是「用力拉、拽」（第 1 个义项：猛地用力拉某物）；句意：小女孩拽着父亲的袖子，急着带他去看那只新来的小狗。

pos.zh: 用力拉；猛拽；艰难地移动
猛拉；一股（强烈的感情）；拖船

derivatives.zh: tug 加 -ing 构成动名词，义为「拉拽；拉扯的动作」
tug 加 boat 构成的复合词，义为「拖船」
tug 加施动者后缀 -er 构成，义为「拉拽者」，多见于游戏与方言

senses.title: To pull hard and sharply
senses.definition: to pull something with a sudden, forceful movement, often several times
senses.definitionCN: 用突然而有力的动作拉某物，常反复拉几次
senses.example: She tugged the heavy door until it finally opened.
senses.exampleCN: 她用力拉那扇沉重的门，直到它终于打开。
senses.why: The oldest use is a hard short pull, and the image of a rope grasped in both hands starts here.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的用法就是短促有力地拉，双手攥绳的意象正是从这里开始。

senses.title: A sharp pull
senses.definition: a sudden hard pull or a single jerk
senses.definitionCN: 一次突然用力的拉扯或拽动
senses.example: He gave the rope a firm tug and the bell rang.
senses.exampleCN: 他猛拉了一下绳子，铃便响了。
senses.why: Any action word can become a noun for one instance of the action, so one pull becomes a tug.
senses.whyCN: 动作词很容易转化为名词，表示一次动作，于是猛地拉一下就叫 a tug。

senses.title: A hard emotional pull
senses.definition: a strong, painful pull on the feelings or conscience
senses.definitionCN: 对感情或良心的强烈而难受的牵扯
senses.example: She felt a tug of guilt as she drove away.
senses.exampleCN: 她驱车离开时，感到一阵内疚的拉扯。
senses.why: Since a tug is a force acting against you, the word naturally describes feelings that pull the heart.
senses.whyCN: 既然 tug 是作用于你的对抗力，这个词自然被用来形容牵扯心神的情绪。

senses.title: A small strong boat
senses.definition: a small but powerful boat used to push or pull larger vessels
senses.definitionCN: 小而动力强、用来推拉大型船只的船
senses.example: A tug guided the liner into the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 一艘拖船引导客轮驶入港口。
senses.why: The boat does one job, pulling heavy ships, so it is simply named after that job.
senses.whyCN: 这种船只干一件事——拖沉重的船，于是干脆以这件事来命名。

intro.en: Tug is first recorded in Middle English as a strong pull or as a rope used for pulling, and it probably grew from the Old English verb teon, to draw or pull.
intro.cn: tug 最早见于中古英语，义为「用力拉」或「［拉东西用的绳索］」，一般认为由古英语动词 teon（拖、拉）逐步演变而来。

items.en: The reconstructed verb teuhan gives the basic idea of dragging something along.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构动词 teuhan 表达了「把某物拖走」的基本含义。

items.en: Teon means to draw or pull, and it is the ancestor of tie.
items.cn: 古英语 teon 意为拖拉，也是 tie 的前身。

items.en: Toggen and tuggen appear with the sense of pulling hard at something.
items.cn: toggen、tuggen 等写法出现，意为使劲拉某物。

items.en: Tug is used for a rope as well as the pull itself, and tug of war names the rope contest.
items.cn: tug 既指拉的动作，也指拉力绳，拔河比赛以 tug of war 命名。

items.en: Steam powered tug boats give the word its boat sense.
items.cn: 蒸汽动力的拖船，让这个词获得了「船」的义项。

items.en: The noun keeps a figurative pull of feeling, as in a tug at the heart.
items.cn: 名词又保留了感情上的「拉扯」这一比喻用法，如心头的牵挂。

note.en: Tug is the sound and shape of a short hard pull, close in form to other pulling words and close in meaning to drag, pull, and jerk.
note.cn: tug 是短促有力拉扯的动作与形象，词形上与其他「拉」词接近，意义上也与 drag、pull、jerk 相邻。

entries.definition: to laugh at someone playfully or unkindly
entries.definitionCN: 取笑；逗弄（只是拼写与 tug 相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a small label fixed to something
entries.definitionCN: 标签；标牌（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a small powerful boat that pulls ships
entries.definitionCN: 拖船（tug 加 boat 构成的复合词）

entries.definition: the act of pulling hard
entries.definitionCN: 拉拽的动作

entries.definition: to move something towards you or along
entries.definitionCN: 拉；牵引（最中性的「拉」，无附加的用力感）

entries.definition: to pull something heavy along the ground
entries.definitionCN: 拖；拽（强调重物在地面上被拉着走）

entries.definition: to pull something suddenly in a short sharp movement
entries.definitionCN: 猛拉；急拽（强调单次动作非常突然）

entries.definition: to pull something heavy with steady effort
entries.definitionCN: 拖运；拉（强调持续用力对付重物）

normalIntro.en: Tug is a short word for a short, hard pull, and it grows into a noun, a boat name, and a word for feelings.
normalIntro.cn: tug 是个短词，专门形容短促有力的拉，由此长出名词、船名，甚至指感情的牵扯。

normal.en: Tug at something means to keep pulling it hard, like a child pulling a sleeve.
normal.cn: tug at 某物就是不停使劲拉它，比如孩子拉着袖子。

normal.en: Tug of war is the rope game where two teams pull in opposite directions.
normal.cn: tug of war 就是两队朝相反方向拽绳子的拔河比赛。

normal.en: A tug boat is so named because its whole job is pulling big ships.
normal.cn: 拖船之所以叫 tug boat，是因为它的全部工作就是拉大船。

normal.en: Word forms double the consonant: tugged and tugging, never tugged with one g.
normal.cn: 词形变化要双写辅音 g：tugged、tugging，不能只写一个 g。

normal.en: Compare pull and drag: tug is a quick hard pull, drag is dragging something heavy.
normal.cn: 对比 pull 与 drag：tug 是短促有力地拉，drag 是拖着沉重的东西走。

abstract.en: Picture two hands gripping a rope, feet braced, leaning back.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手攥紧绳子，双脚死死撑住，身体向后倾斜。

abstract.en: Think of a single sharp movement of the arm that brings a bell to life.
abstract.cn: 想象手臂猛地一使劲，把铃铛拉响。

abstract.en: Imagine a small warm hand closing around your finger and refusing to let go.
abstract.cn: 想象一只温软的小手攥住你的手指，怎么也不肯松开。

examples.en: The child tugged at her mothers coat to stop her leaving.
examples.cn: 孩子拽住母亲的外套，不让她离开。

examples.en: A fleet of tugs hauled the damaged tanker away from the reef.
examples.cn: 一支拖船队把受损的油轮从礁石边拖走了。

examples.en: He felt a sharp tug of homesickness at the sight of the old railway station.
examples.cn: 一见到那座老火车站，他就感到一阵尖锐的思乡之情。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「他ɡ」——使劲「拉」一把，累得直喘气，发出「拖格」一声；记 tug 是用力拉。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 teon（拖、拉）→ 中古英语 tuggen（使劲拉）→ tug（猛拉；拖船；感情的牵引），核心义「短促而有力的拖拽」。

sensesIntro.en: Tug starts with a hard pull, then names one such pull, the boat that pulls, and finally the pull of feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: tug 始于一次用力拉扯，随后指这一次拉拽、专门拉船的小船，最后落到感情的牵扯上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands on a rope, leaning back and pulling.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手攥绳、身体后倾地拉扯。

branches.en: Pulling hard at something is the verb sense.
branches.cn: 使劲拉某物，是动词义项。

branches.en: One hard pull becomes the everyday noun.
branches.cn: 一次用力的拉，成为常见的名词义项。

branches.en: Feelings that pull on the heart extend the physical force.
branches.cn: 牵扯心神的感情，是物理拉力的延伸。

branches.en: The boat and the verb share the same pulling job.
branches.cn: 拖船与动词共享同一件「拉」的差事。

branches.en: Both a jerk and a tug boat name a single pulling force at work.
branches.cn: 一次猛拽和一艘拖船，都指向一种正在发力的牵引。

intro.en: Tug is a short native English word, so its derivations all come from adding endings or combining with other English words.
intro.cn: tug 是地道的英语短词，其派生全部靠加后缀或与其他英语词组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Tug has no Latin source, since it descends from the Old English verb teon; the words listed here are English compounds and endings.
latinIntro.cn: tug 并无拉丁语来源，它出自古英语动词 teon；下面列出的是英语的复合形式与词尾。

items.example: Teon supplies the earliest pulling idea.
items.exampleCN: teon 提供了最早的「拉」义。

items.example: Tug keeps the hard short pull.
items.exampleCN: tug 保留了短促有力的拉。

items.example: Tug also names the act.
items.exampleCN: tug 也指这个动作本身。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms tugging.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 tugging。

items.example: The ending -ed forms tugged.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 tugged。

items.example: The suffix -er forms tugger.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 tugger。

items.example: Boat combines in tugboat.
items.exampleCN: boat 与 tug 组合成 tugboat。

items.example: War combines in tug of war.
items.exampleCN: war 与 tug 组合成拔河的说法。

items.example: Heart appears in the phrase tug at the heartstrings.
items.exampleCN: heart 出现在「拨动心弦」这一说法中。

items.example: Tie shares the same Old English ancestor.
items.exampleCN: tie 与 tug 共享同一个古英语前身。

definition_zh: 拖船；拖轮；小型拖拽船
definition_en: a small but powerful boat that pulls or pushes larger ships into and out of a harbour
core_image: 一艘矮壮的船顶着巨轮侧舷，把庞然大物缓缓拖进窄窄的港湾口
scene: 清晨的港口雾气很重，一艘小小的黄色拖船紧贴着货轮侧舷，慢慢把它推入停泊位。At dawn in the misty harbour, a small yellow tugboat pushed the vast cargo ship slowly into its berth.
sceneCN: 这里 tugboat 是「拖船、拖轮」（第 1 个义项：拖拽大船进出港口的小型强力船）；句意：清晨港口雾大，一艘小黄拖船贴着货轮侧舷，把它慢慢推入泊位。

derivatives.zh: 用力拖拽，tugboat 的动词成分，核心义为「猛力拉」
拖船，与 tugboat 同义，专指在河流与运河中拖带驳船
拖船；猛拉，由动词转来的名词义
拖拽者；牵引装置，由 tug 加表示施动者的词尾构成

senses.title: A small powerful boat that pulls bigger ships
senses.definition: a small, strongly built boat that pulls or pushes large ships when they cannot steer well on their own
senses.definitionCN: 船身较小但动力强劲的船，专门拖拽或推顶无法自主操控的大船
senses.example: The tugboat nudged the freighter gently towards the dock.
senses.exampleCN: 拖船轻轻把货轮推靠码头。
senses.why: Tug is a hard pull, and boat names the craft, so a tugboat is literally a boat built for hard pulling.
senses.whyCN: tug 的意思是「猛力拉」，boat 是「船」，所以 tugboat 字面就是「专门猛力拉拽的船」，核心画面正是小艇用力拖大船。

senses.title: The job of guiding a ship into and out of port
senses.definition: the work a small vessel does when it guides or positions large vessels in narrow harbours
senses.definitionCN: 小型船只把大船引导、调整到狭窄港口泊位的工作
senses.example: Without a tugboat, the ferry could not have entered the narrow channel.
senses.exampleCN: 没有拖船协助，渡轮根本无法进入那条狭窄航道。
senses.why: The boat is named for its pull, and that pull exists only when a big ship needs steering assistance.
senses.whyCN: 这种船以「拉」命名，而「拉」只有在巨轮需要被引导时才发生，所以拖船一词天然带着港口引导作业的场景。

senses.title: Someone or something that pulls others along
senses.titleCN: 像拖船一样带着别人走的人或物
senses.definition: a figure of speech for a person or team that drags a heavier group forward
senses.definitionCN: 比喻意义上，指把更沉重的整体拉着往前走的人或团队
senses.example: The young striker was the tugboat of a struggling team all season.
senses.exampleCN: 整个赛季，这名年轻前锋就是那支疲弱球队的拖船。
senses.why: The image of a small engine moving a huge mass invites a figurative reading for people who lift others.
senses.whyCN: 小引擎拖动能动的大质量，这幅画面自然引申为「身材或地位不大、却把同伴拉起来的人」，也就是球队或团队里的拖船。

intro.en: Tugboat joins tug, a hard pull, to boat, and the compound names a craft built to pull and manoeuvre ships.
intro.cn: tugboat 由 tug（猛拉）与 boat（船）复合而成，专指为拖带与调遣大船而造的小船。

items.en: A reconstructed root behind Slavic and Germanic words means pulling or drawing along.
items.cn: 一般认为，同出这一重构词根的一组日耳曼语与斯拉夫语词都表示拉扯、牵引。

items.en: Standard English makes its first record of tug, a hard pull, from about the 14th century.
items.cn: tug（猛力一拉）一般认为在十四世纪前后首次见于英语记录，较古英语的核心时段更晚。

items.en: Boat arrives from Old English bat, a word also shared with Dutch and German.
items.cn: boat 来自古英语 bat，这一词形与荷兰语、德语中表示船的词同源。

items.en: The compound tugboat appears as steam tugs begin moving coal barges in harbours.
items.cn: 十八世纪起，蒸汽拖船在港口里拖运煤船，tugboat 这一复合词随之出现。

items.en: Tugboat now covers harbour piloting, salvage work and even figurative helpers.
items.cn: 现代英语中，tugboat 既指港口引航与救助作业，也用于比喻甘愿拉人一把的角色。

note.en: Tugboat sits near words for towing at sea, and words that merely look similar.
note.cn: tugboat 与表示「海上拖曳」的单词处在同一语义圈，另有一批只是拼写相近的词需要区分。

entries.definition: to pull something hard and suddenly
entries.definitionCN: 猛力拉扯；拖拽

entries.definition: a word for a type of food or an old noun for a piece of cloth
entries.definitionCN: 食物一类名称或旧义中的布片；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: able to be touched
entries.definitionCN: 可触摸的；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a fishing boat that drags a net behind it
entries.definitionCN: 拖网渔船，靠身后拖网捕鱼，同属「拖」义场

entries.definition: a boat that carries people and goods across water
entries.definitionCN: 渡轮，与人港作业的拖船常在同一港口出现

entries.definition: a long flat cargo boat on canals or rivers
entries.definitionCN: 驳船，常由拖船拖动，属于同一类水上运输

normalIntro.en: Tugboat is a compound: tug is the hard pull, boat is the craft, so picture a small hull built purely for pulling.
normalIntro.cn: tugboat 是复合词：tug 是「猛拉」，boat 是「船」，所以记成一个只为「拉」而生的小船身。

normal.en: Tug means a hard pull, so a tugboat is a boat made for pulling.
normal.cn: tug 意为猛拉，所以 tugboat 就是为拉而生的小船。

normal.en: The plural is regular: one tugboat, two tugboats.
normal.cn: 复数是规则变化：一艘 tugboat，两艘 tugboats。

normal.en: A tugboat works in a harbour, unlike a trawler, which works at sea for fish.
normal.cn: tugboat 在港口作业，而拖网渔船 trawler 在海上捕鱼，场域不同。

normal.en: Tugboat combines with captain, crew and engine to describe people and machinery.
normal.cn: tugboat 可与 captain、crew、engine 组合，分别指拖船船长、船员与发动机。

normal.en: Use tug for the act, as in tug the rope, and tugboat for the vessel.
normal.cn: 动作说 tug，如 tug the rope（拉绳子）；用船时则说 tugboat。

abstract.en: See a small yellow hull pressed against the black flank of a huge ship.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘小小的黄色船身紧贴着黑压压的大船侧舷。

abstract.en: Hear an engine growling low while a rope of water churns behind.
abstract.cn: 想象低沉的引擎声，船尾翻起一道翻滚的白浪。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny goalkeeper who pulls a whole team forward.
abstract.cn: 想象一个身材矮小的球员，却把整支球队拽着往前走。

examples.en: Three tugboats guided the oil tanker carefully through the narrow strait.
examples.cn: 三艘拖船把油轮小心地引过狭窄海峡。

examples.en: The tugboat captain waited for the storm to ease before docking.
examples.cn: 拖船船长等风暴稍缓后才靠港。

examples.en: A special tugboat was used to tow the ship to the dry dock.
examples.cn: 人们用一艘专用拖船把那艘船拖到干船坞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踏过」——踏过大浪、把大船硬拖着走的小船，就是拖船。这只是拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 tug（猛力拉，一般认为十四世纪前后见于记录）+ boat（船，古英语 bat）→ tugboat 拖船；核心义「以强力牵引为业的船」。

sensesIntro.en: Tugboat names the pulling vessel first, then its harbour work, and finally a figurative helper.
sensesIntro.cn: tugboat 先指这种会拖拽的船本身，再指它在港口的引导作业，最后引申为把同伴往前拉的人或物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small hull straining against the flank of a giant ship.
core.cn: 核心意象：小小的船身绷紧着顶住巨轮侧舷。

branches.en: The vessel itself is the concrete anchor sense.
branches.cn: 船本身是最具体、最核心的义项。

branches.en: Herding ships in a port is what the vessel does.
branches.cn: 在港口里调度大船，是这种船以作业为名的义项。

branches.en: Pulling heavy weights for others extends to people.
branches.cn: 替他人拖动重物，可引申到愿意带动同伴的人。

branches.en: The craft and its port duties belong together in a bill of lading.
branches.cn: 被命名的船与它在港口的作业职责，常一起出现在货运场景中。

branches.en: Guiding a ship and guiding a team share the same pull.
branches.cn: 引导巨轮与引导团队，用的是同一种「拉」的力量。

intro.en: Tugboat is formed from a native verb and a native noun, so it carries no Latin or Greek affixes.
intro.cn: tugboat 由一个本土动词与一个本土名词直接组合而成，不含拉丁或希腊词缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for this compound, though Roman harbours used towing craft of their own.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词没有拉丁语来源，不过古罗马港口也有自己的牵引船只。

items.example: The sailors tug the heavy rope together.
items.exampleCN: 水手们一起猛拉粗绳。

items.example: A narrow boat waits beside the quay.
items.exampleCN: 一条窄船停在码头边。

items.example: The tugboat churns the water as it pushes.
items.exampleCN: 拖船一边推动一边翻起水花。

items.example: Two tugboats work the same berth.
items.exampleCN: 两艘拖船在同一个泊位工作。

items.meaning: the person in charge of a vessel
items.example: The tugboat captain radios the pilot.
items.exampleCN: 拖船船长用电台联系引航员。

items.example: The harbour is too shallow for the liner.
items.exampleCN: 港湾对大型邮轮来说太浅了。

items.example: The ending -boat also forms sailboat and ferryboat.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -boat 还能构成 sailboat 与 ferryboat。

items.example: A winch tows the barge out of the lock.
items.exampleCN: 绞盘把驳船拖出船闸。

items.example: The lock gate moved with a sudden tug.
items.exampleCN: 闸门突然一扯就动了。

definition_zh: 郁金香；郁金香花；郁金香球茎
definition_en: a plant with a tall stem and a bright cup-shaped flower that opens in spring
core_image: 春日早晨，一支高高的细茎顶着一只饱满的杯形花冠，在微风里轻轻摇晃
scene: 四月，荷兰田野里成片红色的郁金香沿着水渠一直铺到天边，农夫背着竹篮在花间穿行。In April, whole fields of red tulips stretch along the canals to the horizon, and farmers walk among the flowers with baskets on their backs.
sceneCN: 这里 tulip 是「郁金香」（第 1 个义项：春季开杯形花的球根花卉）；句意：四月荷兰田野里红色郁金香沿水渠铺到天边，农夫背着篮子穿行花间。

derivatives.zh: 郁金香木，指一种纹理漂亮的浅色木材，名称借用了花名
郁金香般的，由 tulip 加表示「像……的」词尾构成
郁金香狂热，指十七世纪荷兰的郁金香投机热潮

senses.title: The spring flower with a cup-shaped head
senses.definition: a garden plant grown from a bulb, with a tall smooth stem and one brilliant cup-shaped bloom opening in spring
senses.definitionCN: 由球茎长出的园艺植物，茎高而光滑，春季开出杯状鲜艳的花朵
senses.example: Every spring the city square is crowded with tulips in red and yellow.
senses.exampleCN: 每年春天，城市广场上都挤满红黄两色的郁金香。
senses.why: The flower is named for the turban it resembles, and the rounded cup shape is exactly what the eyes catch first.
senses.whyCN: 郁金香因花冠形状让人联想到土耳其人的头巾而得名，而圆鼓鼓的杯形花冠正是最先看到的特征，所以这个词直接指向整株花卉。

senses.title: The bulb kept for planting
senses.definition: the small onion-shaped bulb of this plant, sold as a planting unit in autumn
senses.definitionCN: 这种植物洋葱状的小球茎，秋季作为播种材料出售
senses.example: The gardener stored the tulip bulbs in a cool dry shed until October.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁把郁金香球茎存放在阴凉干燥的棚屋里，直到十月。
senses.why: The flower comes from a bulb, so the name easily shifts to the bulb people handle in autumn.
senses.whyCN: 郁金香由球茎长成，所以名称很自然地转到秋季里人们手里那颗球茎上，购买、储存、栽种时都说这个词。

senses.title: The flower as a token of beauty and wealth
senses.titleCN: 象征美与珍宝的郁金香
senses.definition: a symbol of Dutch wealth and, in economic history, the subject of the first recorded market bubble
senses.definitionCN: 作为财富与美的象征，也是经济史上有记载的首个投机泡沫的主角
senses.example: The tulip became a national emblem of the Netherlands.
senses.exampleCN: 郁金香成了荷兰的国家象征。
senses.why: Because the bloom was rare and dazzling, it turned into a traded prize and finally a national emblem.
senses.whyCN: 杯形花冠稀有又耀眼，于是它被当成可以买卖的宝物，进而成为国家的象征，这就是从具体花名长出的抽象义。

intro.en: Tulip is one of several European words that trace back to a Turkish word for turban, carried across the Mediterranean in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: tulip 与几个欧洲语言中的同形词一样，一般认为源于土耳其语中表示「头巾」的词，十六世纪经地中海传入欧洲。

items.en: Ottoman Turkish tülbent means a light muslin cloth or a turban.
items.cn: 奥斯曼土耳其语 tülbent 指轻薄细棉布或包头用的头巾，是这一词族的起点。

items.en: The Turkish cloth word is usually traced to Persian dulband, a turban.
items.cn: 一般认为土耳其语中表示布料的词来自波斯语 dulband（头巾）。

items.en: European scholars recorded tulipa, a plant name with the turban word inside it.
items.cn: 十六世纪的欧洲学者用拉丁语 tulipa 记录这种植物，词中隐含着头巾的含义。

items.en: French tulipan, and later tulipe, spread the plant name across Europe.
items.cn: 法语 tulipan 及后来的 tulipe，把这种植物的名称传播到欧洲各地。

items.en: Tulip enters English around the 1570s as Dutch breeders spread the plant.
items.cn: 十六世纪七十年代前后，随着荷兰育种者推广这种花，tulip 进入英语。

items.en: Modern English uses tulip for the flower, the bulb and the Dutch boom alike.
items.cn: 现代英语用 tulip 兼指花、球茎，以及荷兰的那场郁金香热潮。

note.en: Tulip looks and sounds like a few unrelated words, and shares a field with other spring bulbs.
note.cn: tulip 在拼写和读音上与几个无关词相近，又与其他春季球根花卉同处一个语义圈。

entries.definition: a cloth headdress wrapped closely round the head
entries.definitionCN: 包头巾，是与郁金香同源的词，花名正来自头巾形状

entries.definition: the Dutch speculative craze for tulip bulbs
entries.definitionCN: 郁金香狂热，由 tulip 加表示「狂热」的词尾构成

entries.definition: a light ringing sound
entries.definitionCN: 轻微的叮当声；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a spring flower with a yellow trumpet-shaped centre
entries.definitionCN: 水仙花，同为春季开花的球根植物

entries.definition: a tall plant with large trumpet or cup flowers
entries.definitionCN: 百合，花形与郁金香相近的球根花卉

entries.definition: a rounded underground part that grows into a plant
entries.definitionCN: 球茎，郁金香依靠它在土中越冬

normalIntro.en: Tulip arrives through a Turkish word for turban, so the flower name and the headdress grew from the same root.
normalIntro.cn: tulip 经土耳其语中表示「头巾」的词传入，所以花名与头巾本出一源。

normal.en: Tulip comes from a Turkish word for turban, because the bloom looks like a wrapped head.
normal.cn: tulip 源自土耳其语中「头巾」一词，因为花冠像裹好的头巾。

normal.en: The plural is regular: one tulip, many tulips.
normal.cn: 复数规则变化：一支 tulip，许多 tulips。

normal.en: Tulip pairs with bulb, bed and festival to cover gardening and culture.
normal.cn: tulip 与 bulb、bed、festival 搭配，可涵盖园艺与文化场景。

normal.en: Tulipomania joins tulip to madness and names a famous market bubble.
normal.cn: tulipomania 由 tulip 加表示「狂热」的成分构成，专指那场著名的市场泡沫。

normal.en: Compare lily and daffodil, other bulbs whose names are not transparent.
normal.cn: 对比 lily 与 daffodil：同样是球根花卉，名字却看不出构词线索。

abstract.en: See one tall stem holding a glossy cup that has just opened.
abstract.cn: 想象一根高茎顶着一只刚刚张开的亮亮小杯。

abstract.en: Picture rows of red and yellow cups swaying beside a canal.
abstract.cn: 想象水渠旁一排排红黄小杯随风轻摇。

abstract.en: Think of a sealed envelope of silk folded round a head.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈丝绸像信封一样裹住头顶。

examples.en: She planted tulips along the garden wall last autumn.
examples.cn: 去年秋天，她沿着花园的围墙种了郁金香。

examples.en: The tulip bulbs must be lifted before the ground freezes.
examples.cn: 郁金香球茎必须在地面结冰前挖出来。

examples.en: In the history of finance, the tulip boom is a classic warning tale.
examples.cn: 在金融史上，郁金香热潮是一个经典的警示故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吐丽花」——一吐芬芳、艳丽得像小酒杯的花，就是郁金香。这只是拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 土耳其语 tülbent（细棉布、头巾，一般认为源自波斯语 dulband）→ 拉丁语 tulipa → 法语 tulipe → 英语 tulip，核心义「形似包头巾的花」。

sensesIntro.en: Tulip names the plant first, then the bulb sold for planting, and finally the flower as a cultural symbol.
sensesIntro.cn: tulip 先指整株花卉，再指用于栽种的球茎，最后指作为文化符号的郁金香。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tall stem holding one bright cup-shaped bloom.
core.cn: 核心意象：细高的茎顶着一只鲜艳的杯形花冠。

branches.en: The flowering plant is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 开花植株是最常用的义项。

branches.en: The bulb is the planting unit people buy.
branches.cn: 球茎是人们购买与栽种的单位。

branches.en: The flower as emblem and boom is the cultural sense.
branches.cn: 作为象征与投机对象的郁金香，是文化义项。

branches.en: A planted bulb grows into the bloom everyone recognises.
branches.cn: 种下球茎，长成人人认得的那朵花。

branches.en: Its beauty is why a single flower could command absurd prices.
branches.cn: 正因为它的美，一朵花才能被炒到荒唐的价钱。

intro.en: Tulip is a loan word rather than a suffixed form, so its family is built with English compounds and endings.
intro.cn: tulip 是外来词，不是由词缀拼成的词，因此它的词族由英语复合与词尾扩展而来。

latinIntro.en: The medieval Latin form tulipa carried the Turkish word into European botany.
latinIntro.cn: 中古拉丁语形式 tulipa 把土耳其语词带进了欧洲植物学。

items.example: The tulip opens in early spring.
items.exampleCN: 郁金香在早春开放。

items.example: The tulips along the path are blooming.
items.exampleCN: 小路边的郁金香正盛开。

items.meaningCN: 植物学中的郁金香属名
items.example: Latin tulipa names the genus in botany.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 tulipa 是植物学中的属名。

items.example: French tulipe is the bridge form.
items.exampleCN: 法语 tulipe 是中间的桥梁形式。

items.example: Each tulip bulb carries the next bloom.
items.exampleCN: 每个郁金香球茎都孕育着下一次开花。

items.example: The ending -wood forms tulipwood.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -wood 构成 tulipwood。

items.example: Tulipwood is prized by cabinet makers.
items.exampleCN: 郁金香木很受家具工匠青睐。

items.example: The ending -mania forms tulipomania.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -mania 构成 tulipomania。

items.example: Tulipomania peaked in the 1630s.
items.exampleCN: 郁金香狂热在十七世纪三十年代达到顶峰。

items.example: The turban is the shape behind the name.
items.exampleCN: 头巾是这个名字背后的花形联想。
